body:

I have already contacted support but unfortunately received no response: Tasks that I have long since completed, checked off, and in some cases also hidden keep reappearing in the Inbox, which causes complete chaos in my entire task planning. I have to check them off again every time. I am so sorry that, even though the team is truly making a great effort and doing really wonderful things, the app is unusable for me in this way. title: Gute iOS-/Web-App, sehr schlechte macOS App
body: Nicht falsch verstehen, ich mochte Structured schon vor Jahren. Jetzt wollte ich es wieder benutzen und mir die Lifetime-Version holen, vor allem da es mittlerweile eine macOS-Version gibt und man über die Cloud synchroneren kann. Doch leider bin ich sehr ernüchtert. Die gesamte Bedienung hinkt der Web-App sehr hinterher, es ist richtig lästig zu verwenden. Viele Ansichtsmodi im Web, nur eine einzige in der macOS App, egal wie groß man das Fenster zieht. Das wechseln zwischen Tagen ist nicht möglich, sondern nur zwischen Wochen. Um an einem Sonntag auf morgen zu kommen, müsste man also mehrere Klicks durchführen (nächste Woche, Montag anklicken). Keine Anzeige des Wochentages, dadurch denkt man bei Klick auf den Pfeil rechts, man sehe in der *Tagesansicht* den nächsten Tag. Man sieht an einem Freitag aber den nächsten Freitag und plant völlig falsch, weil man das nicht direkt versteht. Verschieben der Aufgaben zwischen den Tagen ist die absolute Krätze: Aufmachen, Kalender anklicken, Tag suchen, komplett überladen werden von hunderten Icons und trotzdem nicht wissen wohin man will, Ansicht wieder verlassen, superaufwändig den gewünschten Zieltag suchen, dann wieder zurückgehen, Termin anklicken und dann die Zeit mit Dutzenden !!! Klicks einstellen. Warum man sich dazu entschieden hat, fancy UI Bedienelemente vom iPhone auf den Mac zu übernehmen weiß auch kein Mensch. Ich kann von mir aus durch Zeiten scrollen, aber ich will sie auch eingeben können ohne dass ich dafür in ein Kontext-Unter-Untermenü gehen und den Modus (dauerhaft) umschalten muss, nur um festzustellen, dass diese Ansicht mich mit ihren unerklärlichen -/+ Buttons total erschlägt. Man könnte ja meinen „dann nutz doch einfach die Web-App“. Schön, aber da kann ich keine E-Mail reinziehen die in eine Aufgabe verwandelt wird, sondern alles aufwändig mit der Hand eingeben, wie am iPhone. Die gewaltigen Vorteile für eine ernsthafte Nutzung sterben durch das schlechte UI einfach. Ach so, Aufgabenkategorien anyone? Habe meine kategorisierten und priorisierten Erinnerungslisten mit insgesamt nichteinmal 100 Aufgaben synchronisiert, jetzt ist das alles einfach in der Inbox, total durcheinander, ohne Kategorien, Kontext, Listenname oder sonstwas, woran man auch nur irgendetwas erkennen könnte. Mental overload deluxe. Die Inbox bzw. der Sync ist dadurch einfach mal gar nicht mehr brauchbar. Das UI ist simpel, aber unübersichtlich, dafür wenigstens aber lästig und schwerfällig zu bedienen.

title: Has helped me immensely :)
body: I'd recommend Structured to anyone struggling with time management, remembering tasks and important dates or even things as simple as making time for their own needs. My life has genuinely improved since I've started using this app, regarding work just as much as my free time. Planning ahead for the next day has become an important part of my daily routine and has even helped me with sleep problems, since I don't have as many things circling my brain anymore at night – I can just write down whatever it is that I need to remember and put it on my schedule for whenever I have the time and energy. What really sets Structured apart from other similar apps for me is the energy tracker. It allows you to not only see when you have enough time, but also when you're mentally and physically prepared to handle a task. It's an absolute game changer for people who struggle with mental health issues and to whom seemingly simple tasks often feel overwhelming and daunting. Everyday life feels so much more manageable now and I don't think I've ever been this productive :) I can't recommend this app enough!

Ich würde diese App sofort als meine hauptsächliche Kalender App verwenden, wenn die Synchronisation von Kalenderdaten in beide Richtungen funktionieren würde und Anlagen hinzugefügt werden können.

With its intuitive features and user-friendly interface, this app has revolutionized the way I manage my schedule and accomplish my goals. What sets it apart even further is the app's generosity in providing free premium access to those who cannot afford it. One of the first things that impressed me about Structured was its sleek and intuitive interface. The developers have clearly put a lot of thought into the design, making it visually appealing and easy to navigate. The clean layout and well-organized sections allow me to create on my tasks effortlessly. Whether you're a tech-savvy individual or a beginner, the user-friendly interface makes it a breeze to get started and stay organized. It’s worth the subscription

title: Danke für diese super App!
body: Nutze diese App erst seit wenigen Monaten, doch ich bin begeistert! Die Integration und dann auch laufende Synchronisation von Apple Reminders und deinem Kalender in structured ist ein Feature, welches mir in so vielen anderen Apps fehlt! Design sehr schön und ansprechend gestaltet und auch die Möglichkeit farbliche Anpassungen vorzunehmen gefällt mir sehr! Pro zahlt sich für mich zu 100% aus! Leider funktioniert die Synchronisation bei mir am iPad manchmal ein wenig schlecht, was ich aber beheben kann, indem ich in denEinstellungen die Synchronisation für bestimme Kalender-Events und Reminders aus- und dann wieder einschalte. Schön wäre natürlich ein Überblick über die nächste Woche bzw. Monat und eine "Rück"-Synchronisation zum Kalender und den Reminders, um in structured erstellte Tasks und Events dort auch im Blick zu haben, doch auch jetzt schon gibt es von mir 5/5 Sterne!

Auch wäre es toll, wenn man in der Hauptansicht selbst und nicht so umständlich wie bislang (Klick auf Task → Fenster erscheint → Aufgabe bearbeiten klicken → Bearbeitungsfenster erscheint) die Aufgaben bearbeiten könnte...

title: ADHD Time Blindness
body:
Might be the best app ever for daily planning, especially if you have ADHD and struggles with time blindness or the friction of manually planning your day. 

The app makes it so easy to set up routines and adapt to your day thanks to the AI as well as the hourglass timeline that constantly updates with time.

The focus timer has helped me a lot with focusing on current tasks and not get sidetracked. With the recent addition of automated intervals, it’s even way more useful! 

Really is the perfect daily planning app for ADHDers !!! I HOPE THE CREATORS MAINTAIN THIS APP FOREVER ESPECIALLY WITH THE LIFETIME SUPSCRIPTION BEING AVAILABLE

body:

- IOS 26
- Coincidently (maybe?) my other app (NextThere) has the exact same issue (see issue below)
- I click on the app (Structured), the Structured logo (the pink tick) appears in the centre of my screen surrounded by blackness for 1 second then the app crashes. If I click on the app after it crashes the same thing happens, the logo appears then the app crashes. Always the same.
- I CAN use the app on my MacBook air (without any problem), but my app (on my iPhone) is what I use all the time. I almost never use Structured on my MacBook Air. 

I use this app so much. Has helped with my ADHD diagnoses.  If you need anymore info please let me know?! Thanks!

title: Best free calendar application in all of the internet
body: Before using this, i used a physical diary. A physical diary is impractical as to carry it everywhere along with a pen plus it’s limited space and also my life became more demanding which prompted me to find an alternative. I tried a couple of calendar apps but I’ll spare you the details. Essentially, this app was the best. Other apps asked for a paid subscription and if you didn’t, you wouldn’t access to basic features such as being able set alerts once an event begins(ironic because this feature is also limited in this program but ill get to it). The ability to EASILY drag tasks/events to certain times or days, was a feature that really is intuitive and I think would make a difference in the 90% of people reading this review. Not only that but what they call “inbox” in this program also doubles down as a to-do list which is incredibly handy. Having one app that takes all these needs is super beneficial. However I would give this program a 4.8/5 if they was an option. And that is the ability to being able to set alerts prior to an event/task AND able to repeat events. Of course if you pay for their paid subscription, you’ll get these features. However, I believe that these two are fundamental features to a calander app and I know for a lot of people, it can be a deal breaker, if they dont have one or both of these features. Other than that though, no complaints whatsover. title: Great for my silly lil Neurospicy brain
body:
I massively struggle with time management and task hopping due to my ADHD, even with medication, and am constantly making & losing track of to-do lists. Structured helps me prioritise tasks, colour code the things I need to for uni/work/personal life/medical needs etc, gives me much needed timely reminders AND I get a fun little dopamine reward boost every time I check something off. My fave feature is the inbox; whenever I think of something I need to do I can just jot it down in the moment without having to commit to when to do it, and then when I have the mental capacity to organise myself I can easily transfer it into the calendar. I also love the cute suggestions for small time gaps - yah I absolutely do want a stretch/snack, thank you, I forgot to eat and take care of myself again oops 🫠

The only gripe I have is that when I delete an event in my Apple calendar that has already transferred to structured, it doesn’t also update the event in the structured app, so I end up having to edit two calendars. But that might be due to my rather embarrassing inability to work technology so take it as you will. Yeah I forget to use it for days at a time, but I still love it. 10/10 would recommend.

I love the fact that you can connect the One Sec app and it caters for people who are dyslexic. This is seriously an app that cares for people! I’m looking to get the full version now as I’ve been using excel spreadsheets to organize my life (and I’m paying for excel…) at least here it’s so much more user friendly and multifunctional!

title: Reality check on timings
body:
I have used this app on and off for a while now and just recently paid for an annual access to try the AI planner.  I have to say… wow! This app is the pinnacle of brilliant UX/UI.  I’m ADHD (was diagnosed before the smart phone was invented :p) and my concept of time has always been terrible.  This app allows me to see the reality of how long it takes to do things and visually shows me where I need to take breaks or allow a buffer zone for timings. The AI app allows you to use your voice to plan things so even if you have planned your morning you can add stuff like “after 12pm I need to do ‘x’, then ‘y for 30mins’ etc”.  
The only suggestion I would make is allowing your inbox to have subcategories so you don’t have to switch over to the reminders app, e.g priority tasks. 
Brilliant! Just download it and try it, even the free version is great!

title: Actually changed my life
body:
I love this app. I am scatterbrained and can't remember what I need to do half the time, but this app really helps me get stuff done. When I think of something I need to do, instead of worrying about it, I pop it in the inbox section so I can schedule it later. Then all my tasks are right there in the morning for me to schedule in for the day. 

The visual layout also helps me understand how much time I have and how long something will take. This stops me from overcommitting myself and feeling guilty about uncompleted tasks later.

I have tried diaries, planners, do to lists, calendars, you name it, but nothing consistently worked for me. This app works because it's always with me on my phone, and it looks nice and is easy to use. It's amazing now that I get things done and can remember all my responsibilities!

Thanks for making this app!

title: Great App. Definitely Recommend. Although I do have some suggested improvements 😊
body:
Definitely would recommend this app. It's great to be able to just see everything that I have on that day in one place. Also the inbox is very helpful to be able to see what tasks I have that need doing, but also being able to put them somewhere to find the time. 

This is a great app trust me but I do have some suggestions to improve it for a better user experience. One improvement I could think of would be instead of just saying that the tasks overlap, put them side by side, kind of in two columns, so that I can see by how much they actually do overlap and then you could put the line that marks where the time is up to across both tasks. The second improvement would be to be able zoom out on my day just to be able to see all my tasks right next to each other rather than spaced out along the timeline, still being able to see what the tasks are, but just all beside each other. Another improvement would be when the notification comes up for a task, the option to either start the task now or delay for 5 - 10 minutes. It often happens that I plan a task, but overestimated how long it would take to finish the task before, so this feature would be helpful for delaying tasks. 

Also, more icons for tasks would be great too 😊

This is an amazing app, especially considering I haven't purchased the pro version as of yet definitely considering that. Although, the free version works quite well too.

title: Too much clicking
body:
Loving the idea of integrating to-do list and timeline. However, after trying this app for a week I started to feel its a bit tedious to use. 

For example, when I want to add a task that has been created in the inbox to today's timeline, I have to: 1)Click the   button; 2) Scroll to pick a time when the task should start; 3) Click to choose the duration of the task; 4) Most of the time in my case, tasks last for longer than 1.5h, which is the longest one provided by default, so I have to click on 'More', click and type in 'hour', click and type in 'min', and I can't use tab to move from 'hour' to 'min' as it just allows me to type more space in the 'hour' textbox! After all these I need to click on 'Add Task' to complete the process. If I want to modify the task after adding it to timeline, I have to go through all these again! 

Some suggestions/feature requests:
1. It would be very useful if I can just drag the task from inbox, drop it to a desired starting time in the timeline. By doing so it will create a block on my timeline with a duration of one hour by default. And then I can extend or shorten the duration by draging the bottom of the block.
2. Remove tasks from timeline back to inbox, by drag-and-drop ideally.

I like this app and would like to see it gets better! Keep it up!

body:

Another small pet peeve i have with the app is if i got a task scheduled between 1-8pm, and dinner scheduled at 5pm, then “dinner “just cut through the “work” task. It would be awesome if you can show overlap visually, as in “dinner” task is overlapping “work” task instead of cutting it, rather than as a small icon next to the task to indicate there is overlapped

Last but not least, it doesn't sync across my ipad and iphone for some reasons, even tho i tried to sync it with icloud, or reinstall it, it wont sync. It’s a shame tho, because it would be so convenient to transfer task across. 

Overall, i really like this app. I can see the potential in it! Wishing you guys all the best

L’encodage des tâches est très facile et l’IA peut (parfois) aider à planifier son horaire. Bref, je suis sous le charme. Il manque juste un bouton de raccourci pour revenir à « Aujourd’hui ». On peut le faire par la fenêtre « calendrier », mais ce n’est pas très pratique. Bravo aux développeurs.

title: Juste parfaite
body:
Cette appli permet aux plus désorganisés de se structurer et construire des journées adaptées en un clin d'oeil.
J'ai pu planifier des habitudes et m'y tenir, tout en souplesse. Elle est esthétique, adaptable à l'infini, et redonne plaisir à l'organisation de séances de travail en profondeur, alternées par des sorties et la planification de tout ce qui rempli vos journées. En un coup d'oeil on prend conscience du temps qu'on accorde à chaque sphère de notre vie, et du temps qu'on gagne pour le "redistribuer".
La synchro avec les différents agendas permet, pour moi qui le partage avec mon mari et mes enfants, de voir ce qui sera à remanier pour cadrer à nos horaires à tous. Bref. Parfait pour moi.

title: Nice!
body:
After months of searching and buying planners which were not worth it, I finally think I found the one! 

As it’s still quite new, there is still room for improvement, but I think it has a lot of potential. 

Some ideas of what I’m searching in a planner
- A habit tracker would be handy. Something very simple in the form of a table, where you can just fill in the habit, the days, and a checkbox for when it’s done

- A place to plan workouts. For example you can create a task called workout & link it to the specific workout (where this would then be a page with the workout explained, like a notes page) OR if you want to keep it simple (Which is sometimes better), just the option to have notes

title: É bonito, mas…
body: Acho um dos apps mais bonitos da App Store, porém ele não é prático. Há etapas demais para atualizar tarefas, não há menus rápidos (pelo menos intuitivamente). O foco principal aqui são as tarefas com horário definido, mas as tarefas de dia inteiro são bastante relegadas ao segundo plano; a visibilidade delas também não é boa e você não consegue fazer com que elas sumam após serem concluídas, deixando a área de trabalho poluída demais. Mesmo assim, estou dando 3 estrelas e comprei a versão paga porque acredito que temos um potencial incrível aqui. Basta que o foco seja expandido para outros tipos de usuários. Aliás, eu também tenho outro app do mesmo desenvolvedor que tem o mesmo problema de enxergar apenas um nicho específico e que se dane o resto. O Awake é um ótimo despertador, mas não passa disso também. Você não consegue criar alarmes que não seja despertadores de forma intuitiva e fácil. Entendo que se expandirem o público, as vendas serão impactadas positivamente. “Contrua e eles virão˜.

title: Great, but the free plan could have some improvements
body:
The app is very good, I appreciate the fact that you have improved it and are open to constructive criticism. I didn’t want to change apps, because I love structured, but I can’t pay for the pro plan. Since the pro version already includes so many improvements that boost the app (even AI), the free version should be complemented with nothing more than the basics for simple organization:
You should have the option to synchronize with the free calendar (to make it more easy to organize their routine, since most people already have a rought outline of it in their calendar, but want to move o a better app.)or you don’t need to keep setting up the list every day. It should be able to customize a weekly routine for free. It’s a lot of work in the free version to be putting together the list every day.
Thank you for your attention! 😊😊

title: Aplicativo ótimo, porém…
body: É um ótimo aplicativo. É clean e de fácil uso. Sobre isso, não tenho do que reclamar. É fácil criar e remover tarefas e até mesmo personalizar as mesmas com ícones e cores. O grande problema aqui é o custo do aplicativo lifetime. Pelo preço que cobram, deixo como sugestão aos desenvolvedores que criem algo para todas as plataformas. E se eu tiver que planejar a minha semana e não estiver podendo usar o meu smartphone no momento? Poderia planejar usando meu PC, mas não é possível pela falta da aplicação até mesmo em versão web. O aplicativo tem muito potencial para captar novos usuários e faturar mais, só que provavelmente irão se deparar com usuários como eu, que julgam não valer a pena pagar o que cobram na versão lifetime, pois a mesma só está disponível para iOS e se não me engano, macOS. Se isso que sugeri acontecer, penso mais seriamente em comprar o aplicativo. Enquanto isso, vai depender da minha paciência em relação à ficar copiando tarefas e adicionando aos outros dias da semana, já que programar a mesma para se repetir está disponível apenas mediante pagamento/assinatura. Quando a paciência acabar, devo ir atrás de outro aplicativo, que se não for multiplataforma, talvez seja pelo menos mais condizente o valor lifetime, caso disponível.

body:

The UI is simple and easy to use, the icons have a great design and offers a lot of options to personalize the tasks, including multiple timers. The pro features allow to connect multiples calendars and add recurring tasks, so I can manage my entire day through this app. 
The app offers an option to request the pro features for free, I've requested it since the price is too high in my country and it really worked! 
Many thanks to the Structured team ❤️

title: Day 2 of my trial and I’m NOT subscribing when it ends
body:
I really wanted to like Structured because it advertises itself as being especially helpful for people with ADHD. Unfortunately, my experience during the trial was the opposite.

The AI was the main reason I considered paying for the app, but it ended up creating more work instead of saving me time. I would ask it to schedule tasks, then have to go back and manually fix the schedule. When I asked it to move a multi-step outing (such as a library trip with walking there, signing up for library cards, browsing, and walking home), it only moved one task and left the others behind. That completely broke the plan and forced me to reorganize everything myself.

Recurring tasks were another major frustration. When I tried to delete a recurring task, I wasn’t given the expected options to delete just one occurrence, all future occurrences, or the entire series. Instead, I had to edit the recurrence before I could finally remove it. That’s confusing and unnecessarily time-consuming.

Importing Apple Reminders was another disappointing experience. I have well-organized reminder lists with headings, tasks, and subtasks. Structured completely flattened everything during the import, splitting headings, tasks, and subtasks into individual inbox items. Instead of preserving the organization, it created a cluttered mess.

To make matters worse, there was no way to select those imported items as a group and hide or remove them. I had to tap each one individually. The only workaround I found was going into the app’s settings and manually disabling each Reminders list one by one. Even then, one of the lists continued appearing in my inbox after it had been turned off. I had to repeatedly enable and disable the list before Structured finally removed those items.

The app also advertises swipe gestures to quickly delete, postpone, or manage tasks, but those gestures didn’t work for me at all.

After spending my trial fighting with the AI, fixing broken schedules, cleaning up imported reminders, and manually reorganizing tasks, I realized I could accomplish the same thing by using Apple Calendar alongside Reminders. The AI was supposed to be the feature that justified the subscription, but in my experience it wasn’t reliable enough to do that.

The concept behind Structured is excellent, and I can see why people are excited about it. However, the current AI and task management experience simply wasn’t dependable enough for me to trust with my daily planning. Instead of reducing my mental load, it increased it.

title: Brilliant Use of AI
body: I have a lot of issues with staying on taks, or splitting up my day to tackle several large tasks. I tend to just throw myself into a single thing and lose sight that multiple projects and things need to get done, and I end up poorly managing my time. This app really helps with that. Now, I spent five minutes in the morning planning out my day in my journal, making a list, jotting down my durations, and then I hope into structure and use the AI assistant. I feed it the list and then give it parameters like durations, gaps, lunch breaks, and specify where subtasks should go. It all takes less than five minutes, and the app builds out my day and plans it to the minute. What’s even better is if something comes up during the day, I can hope into the AI assistant and get it to rebuild my day making adjustments for completed tasks, etc. It’s really been a game changer for me. And I don’t need to use it every day, just the days where  I really need to be on point and focused. And I love that I can build it all out on my laptop, and then have my phone remind me as I’m running around working of when I should be switching focuses, or even taking breaks. Worth every cent.

title: Useful. However Causes Excess Battery Drain
body: Honestly, this is a really good application. I really love the UI and it’s pretty easy to use. I especially love how there is a Web version which allows me to use it for my day to day planning at work. Overall it’s intuitive and very good for people who like to stay organized and use daily planners. The one caveat with this application and the only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars (and also the reason I am on the fence about subscribing for it) is the battery drain on this app. It appears that this application has NOT been optimized AT ALL for battery efficiency. I am on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, my battery is fantastic. That said - THIS APP DRAINS IT. After several days of usage, I’ve been able to determine it drains about 0.36% of battery per minute. Which I mean, doesn’t seem like much at first glance. But when you run the math on it, that means just using this app for about 25ish minutes a day will drain 10% of your battery.. That’s a lot for a todo/daily planner application. The first day I got the app and I set up my schedule and all my repeating tasks, I used the app for about 1 hour and 5 minutes of screen on time, that resulted in 25% battery usage. To be blunt, that’s horrendously poor optimization. Just for perspective, highly resource intensive applications such as BlackMagic Camera when filming in 60 FPS at 4K use the EXACT SAME amount of battery as this application per minute. There is no reason a daily planner should drain just as much and sometimes more than a highly intensive and resource demanding video recording application. This should definitely be investigated.

title: Good App: Why 4 Stars?
body:
Hi, I’m from Canada. I hardly write any reviews but it kept asking me for one.. so here I am. I’m gonna keep it short, here are 3 main reasons why I like using this app as someone who’s been using it for about 4 years now. 

1. Organization
2. Discipline 
3. Structured App + Notion App = best combo
————————————
1. It helps me stay organized for my daily tasks and simple tasks that I plan to do. 

2. It does help me to stay disciplined for the gym, my walks and my runs. I use it more as a fitness schedule, but you can use it for pretty much everything. 

3. As a first-year college student, using this app for my fitness schedule and the Notion app for my school schedule and as an assignment tracker is one of the best combos.

(Also, sometimes I do get frustrated when certain apps that I would like to use are hard to use, so it’s good because this app is very easy to use.)
————————————
Why 4 stars? 
-The prices of the in-app purchases are too high for students. We don’t have money like that. Not everyone can afford to pay for it. So, I would like to suggest if you guys could do student prices, it would help some of us.

Bye.

title: Promising App with one critical flaw
body:
I’ve been using this app for a month now, and it’s been a great experience so far. I love its clean, minimalistic design, and the reminders are incredibly helpful. I’ve tried multiple productivity apps in the past, but this is the only one I’ve consistently used for a full month.

However, I have one major criticism. I relied heavily on the Copy Day function, but it was recently removed from my app. While I haven’t paid for the app yet, I definitely would have in the future. Losing this feature has made daily task creation much more tedious, to the point where I sometimes skip using the app altogether. It now feels like more of a struggle, and I find myself less inclined to open it.

I really hope the Copy Day feature gets restored soon—it’s a key part of what made this app so effective for me. If it comes back, I’d be happy to continue using (and potentially subscribing to) the app daily again.

title: Not encouraging!
body:
Overall, it's a decent app, but it's not very encouraging! After checking everything off, you don't even get a "well done" or "you did great today." People need that kind of motivation, especially when their schedule is tight and hard. It’s crucial for those with ADHD, procrastination issues, or anxiety to feel motivated to finish tasks.

Also, if you spend 40 minutes doing nothing, it shows "Zzz," making you feel guilty and lazy. Who designed this?!

There's no sense of reward, like you're just expected to get things done like a robot.

Even though I like the organized layout, I don't enjoy using it because it makes me feel rushed and not good enough. No matter how much I get done, I still feel like I'm not good enough, and that's a worse feeling.

I always have a big to do list, but never have I had one that has helped me use allotted time slots. This for some reason works better for me, and it keeps things visually organized and simple. 

This app along with a small ounce of dedication or “want” to change is all you need. It def helped me build my discipline, which like everything else is a practice. 

Also the new AI feature saves a lot of time, especially if I start my day early or late, I can ask to push my daily schedule back however I need it to etc. 

Buying a lifetime membership once my one year is over :)

title: Great but...
body:
I never write reviews but I felt the need to for this app. It's great, I love it. If a reader is debating whether or not to give it a try, you should, design, interface, intuitiveness, features, etc, it's solid.

That being said, there are a few features that would really put it over the top and for me, would justify the annual subscription.
1) I sometimes like to move tasks around the day by dragging them - which the app does perfectly. However it's really difficult to drop it precisely where i want (example at the start time I want) because of the collapsible nature of the schedule. Ideally the day's layout would expand fully when modifying the schedule
2) Would be great if i could drag multiple tasks at the same time, say I'm running late and want to push everything back by 30min, currently it seems the only way to do this is one by one which is a bit tedious
3) Would also be great if i could drag the upper/lower edge of the task bubble on the planner view to make it start earlier or finish later without moving the bubble entirely. Currently i would have to open the task and edit it. not a big deal but something i'd appreciate

on a side note, the macOS version doesn't seem to be showing the task i just created from the macOS version itself, even though it syncs and is visible on my ios version. Admittedly, i'm on macOS 14.4 so maybe i just need to update to the latest version to fix this.

Hope the feedback might be useful to the devs! Otherwise, love the app, keep it up!

title: Can’t say enough great things!
body:
I’ve been using this app for a couple of years now and it has been so helpful for me! As someone that is chronically unorganized, to be able to visualize my tasks as well as see how long they are going to take it’s been a lifesaver for me. Being able to list my tasks for the next day before I go to bed at night and be able to allocate enough time between each quite literally helps me sleep at night and feel prepared to start the next day. As a student with a full time job, it’s hard for me to break up my studying time as well as having time to complete projects, essays, etc. on top of working, but again, this app has been my holy grail!

It also helps as someone with anxiety when it comes to time management and fear of being late, Structured has helped to ease my mind in so many ways and help me hold myself accountable when completing tasks (I’m also bad for procrastinating)

The team at Structured is one I can only dream that every app would have, you guys are the best and thank you for such an amazing app!

title: Insanely Good for Managing Chaos
body: I've tried all the other methods of scheduling/keeping track of tasks. This takes the cake by far. It's minimalistic and the UI is not overwhelming, but it's not super simple that it feels boring. It allows you to focus on the day and gives you just enough of a sneak peek to the days ahead without dumping too much or blindsiding you. I don't get side tracked, I can add subtasks to split up big tasks into smaller more manageable ones. Everything is as minimalistic yet customizable as I'd like it to be (colours, icons, which Reminder categories you can sync, etc.) while being perfectly structured (unlike other apps like Notion, which are overwhelming and lead you to sink time into purely aesthetic/customizability/design). I signed up for the yearly subscription using the 50% off scholarship and it's been amazing!!!

title: Lacks Most Basic Functionalities
body:
I needed calendar integration, so I upgraded to a yearly subscription.  I utterly regretted 2 mins after starting using the app.  It lacks the most basic day-to-day functionalities one would expect from any task management app.  For starters, there is no search function whatsoever!  I couldn’t believe that until I got the confirmation from the help section of the developer’s own website.  NO SEARCH AND NO LIST VIEW.  This means you’d better REMEMBER every task you ever created.  God forbids, if you ever want to look up a specific task, you’ll actually need to flip through every day, one day at a time.  That ALONE would render the app completely useless.  But it gets worse.  There’s no “back to today” either.  You’ll literally have to pull up the calendar and find today’s date to click on.   And the whole flow to create a task is awkward too.  I created a few tasks without realizing the wrong date was selected.  Then afterwards, of course I couldn’t find them.  Remember, NO SEARCH and NO LIST VIEW!  I flipped through weeks worth of daily tasks to locate them.

I’m genuinely shocked at the overwhelmingly positive reviews for such an instantly laughably useless app.  I would say daily view, which is the only view, does look pleasing to the eyes.  I guess a lot of people have tons of time looking at a pretty planner and nothing important to do, because if they do have any real tasks, the planner isn’t going to help them accomplish them.

title: Good, but I do have a few suggestions
body:
I am enjoying the app so far, I do feel that it could definitely be benificial towards my overall productivity. 

The idea of this "AI assistant" is really cool (in theory). I understand that it's currently in beta/alpha, but there are many issues with how it implements activities into my schedule, sometimes skipping over them or not assigning them for the specified amounts of time. 

I also think it would be cool if you can simply give all your tasks to the AI bot, maybe even upload the documents so it could scan them, and plan out a schedule that goes past the timeline of the current day. (three parts of an essay on three different days, setting due dates, etc.)

Finally, I would like there to be some way that this "energy level" idea could be further personalized. I think there should be some sort of question at the end of each assignment where it asks you how much energy this task took from you, and it should try to give you some ways to determine how much energy was used up.

Overall, a great app for productivity. However, there are still ways that I would like to see it become further improved.

author: Aisha.wav

title: Please slow more allow one notification sound! Would be soo much more useful!
body:
I have adhd, but also ASD and OCD, but because of a neurological injury, I have short term memory loss and it looks like severe ADHD. It’s driving me insane. This app would be perfect, exactly what I need, if only I could do more than one sound. Unfortunately, even on the most annoying one, my brain has tuned it out when I’m overwhelmed and my SPD is in overload, and I don’t hear it anymore. The problem is it just neighs all day unless I make there are way less tasks, but then it’s no longer of use because I won’t remember what I need to do. 

It’s either select complete on them all, even if I haven’t done them, just to make the noise stop, or my brain will just turn off anyway and ignore it subconsciously. The biggest issue is that I never know what each neigh is for without picking up my phone and then… I’ve picked up my phone. And I start trying to accomplish things on there, but instantly forget what I was doing and end up going in loops and getting distracted, trying to remember what I was doing, and ultimately  completing basically nothing. Yes, I see the notifications then, but it doesn’t pull me away from the doomsday scroll or starting 500 things on my phone I needed to do, but never finish. I have issues with hyperfocus not just because of adhd but because of the autism and ocd as well, so I do not want to touch my phone. Yes, I know there’s a blocking feature, but I have many reasons why I need that to not be there. Kids being the big one. Didn't work for me.

Anyway, long story short- please add the ability to use more than one sound just like the colours!!  Auditory prompts are so helpful! But as primarily visual currently, I am still just relying on Alexa which is.. a  nightmare, lol. She never stops when asked or gets things right, and my kids try to turn off before I can’t even hear or rememebr what I was even supposed to do anyway. Today has been a perfect example of this, so here I am at this app again and wishing so much that this feature existed because I’m discouraged. 

An app like this is a life saver- it just needs a few tweaks! 🙏🏻 Otherwise it’s great!

title: I'm trying to get there…
body: I have tried structured only a couple of days now, being careful not to use it, because I'm afraid of the costs. I was an RN in Canada then I had an accident in which I crushed both my knees (patellas) now since 2012 I have been on long-term disability. I just had another surgery in which the surgeon was supposed to replace my second knee but when doing so he broke my Femur. Which I've had to buy special braces for my legs with no assistance. I'm so thankful to structured for giving me the chance to let me use their APP. With a discount. I also was just in the hospital before this surgery due to a nervous break down. So concentrating and remembering are not as easy as as it used to be. I'm on medications for that which makes it hard for me to concentrate and Remember things. I have many appointments coming up for more X-rays because they think all my hardware from my most recent surgery failed and “collapsed”. Like I said I haven't used structured a lot because of my money problems but would love to give it a try. I know I'm asking a lot but in 7-8 months hopefully, I can pay 40.00 CAD for a lifetime of use. Then maybe I can help others who are having difficult time in the future as I am, now. I look forward to seeing if this APP will be possible for me. I love the App. I think it would be of great assistance to me not always everyday maybe but most days I will need to get things out of my jumbled head and use this app. Can't wait for some organization! Thanks STRUCTURED!

I can also hold and drag tasks to adjust the time after adding it. This is one of the top accessible apps when it comes to productivity for me. Even the free version is helpful compared to others that make me uninstall because of the bad pricing. I decided to get the monthly then I'm getting the lifetime soon because it's affordable. I've tried many apps like these and never had to write a review until now. This app is worth it and can be used on other devices as well.

body:
Structured is an exceptional daily planner that truly stands out. Its remarkable features, including reoccurring tasks, seamless integration with Apple reminders and calendar, and high customization options, make it an invaluable tool for organizing one's daily life.

One of the most impressive aspects is its flawless performance - no glitches or bugs to be found. The interface is clean, intuitive, and a pleasure to navigate.

Having used this app for two years, I recently had the opportunity to reach out to the developer with questions about accessing the Structured Pro version. The developer's response was not only prompt but also incredibly kind and informative, showcasing a genuine commitment to user satisfaction. 

I can wholeheartedly recommend this app to anyone seeking to enhance their organizational skills. It's a game-changer!

title: Nice App, but room to improve it
body:
I like this application, Ive been using it for roughly 48 hours now and its a clean user-friendly planner. However there is some room to improve here on this application to take this to a 5-star...

1. the mobile app shows bubbles under each of the days where events occur... I have 5 reoccuring events each day causing this top bar to be an absolute UI mess with zero purpose for me now. I would really like a way to toggle this feature on/off in the settings. For people like me that have so many events each day, I want the bubbles to disappear from my calendar-week Ui bar, that way there is nothing there to distract me.

2. Although this app is available on Mac, I can say it is really not optimized properly for it. It takes several clicks on any part of the Ui for the app to recognize a user input request. Ive had instances where Ive had to mash the mouse click on the add button for the app to recognize that I want to create a new event.

3. The introduction needs to be redesigned. Im not super pleased that the system introduces you to its features by adding a bunch of random tasks to your planner -- forcing the end user to have to manually delete each event first before getting the opportunity to start building their planner. its unavoidable, its a UX nightmare, and it frustrates me. Please just switch this to a simple walk-through and give users a blank slate.

4. You have a good opportunity here to also build in some feature that supports habit tracking and displaying that to end users... I want to see how many times this week I completed my "Daily Workout" task in my planner. I want to see how many times I missed checking off the "Cook Dinner" task! At the end of the month this will help me visualize my habits and tailor my next-months planner to it.

Overall, this app is a wonderful app with some areas of improvement. I truly believe that if you consider my feedback and that of your other users then you are on the fast-track to making this one of the top applications on App Store.

body:

That way when I move a task by dragging it, it would bump flexible tasks out of the way but fixed tasks would stay in place. If my moved task conflicts with a fixed task a popup warning can tell me that so I can either fix it or not.

Otherwise the app is awesome! I hope you take my suggestions.

title: Read for idea
body:
Amasing! 
It would be very interesting if we could check a button that would prioritize a task, such as an important appointment. If this button is checked, the task could sound like an alarm on the cell phone and also be added to the calendar section to give a more global overview of important appointments. Also, in the same idea, a checkbox that makes a task more "for informational purposes", a bit like a note or comment, which still allows you to place other tasks in this place.

Traduction: Ça serait très intéressant si nous pouvions cocher une case qui permettrait de prioriser une tâche, comme un rendez-vous important. Si cette case est cochée la tâche pourrait sonner comme une alarme sur le cellulaire et aussi être rajoutée dans la section calendrier pour donner un aperçu plus global des rendez-vous important.  Aussi, dans la même idée, une case à cocher qui rend une tâche plus « a titre informative », un peu comme une note ou un commentaire, qui permet quand même de placer d’autres tâches à cet endroit.

title: Loving this app so far! Some tiny areas for improvement
body:
Thoroughly enjoying using this to plan out my day and have been able to get through more of my tasks when using this! It makes me commit to getting the tasks done at a specific time during the day. 

Small suggestions: 
It would be amazing if there was a button to switch quickly between full and simplified views, as I like to use one view to plan my day (full) and the other when I’m actually going through the day (simplified). Another option is to have the ability to add tasks to a specific gap of free time in simplified view just by clicking on that area (like in full view). 

My other suggestion is having the option of a completion sound (like the Microsoft todo app) when a task is done! Nothing quite motivates me as getting the “ding” sound of completion! 

Overall, really great app that I would recommend to those who have a hard time prioritizing or getting through their tasks!

title: Great for visual planning helpful with ADHD and executive functions
body:
This has helped with my ADHD and issues with executive functions. I've been working on implementing this with my wife and kids as well as my own routines and work projects. Having this across all devices, very reasonable price point, and the focus mode on current tasks are fantastic. This has been a game changer. 

I do have some notes on improving things on the desktop, and perhaps mobile too? It does get a bit busy when adding multiples things and calendars. As I mentioned I'm using this to also plan with my family schedule so things often overlap. 

MAKE THE CURRENT TIME MORE EVIDENT. Perhaps a subtle background block or gradient progressing the entirety of the app background as the daily time progresses, or a simple line through main area mivng with the current time, maybe a solid container around the current time as well using the chosen app colour? 

OVERAPPING ITEMS. I think it would be helpful to make the overlap more evident. Perhaps indicate how much time the overlap is "Tasks are overlapping by 15 mins" and have the times it's overlapping on the left for example. Could you look at indenting the overlapping tasks, or having them display side by side, or collapsable as a group? Maybe an option to toggle specific calendars more easily? 

CHECKLIST INDICATION. The icon is a bit misleading being a solid grey box with a checkmark even though it shows the tally of items check via text beside it. THis makes me think those items are checked off, just a visual thing for me. Perhaps a drop down arrow in the box instead? Or using the outline version of the checkbox icon instead of solid?

Just suggestions from someone with ADHD and being very visual. Seeing time displayed this way is great. More visual the better!

title: Please add a routines option!
body: Please add an option to have repeating and separate routines. I only need this for certain routines, not my entire day. For my ADHD I really need to be able to plan my morning routine on the fly and change it super easily- sometimes even WHILE I’m doing the routine. I would love to see an option to edit the time of a task on the main page and then have the other tasks automatically correlate. So for example if I only take 5 minutes to get dressed instead of 10, all the following tasks begin earlier and the app should update the estimated completion time. I would also love to see estimated completion time in minutes/hours, not just the time of day. That way if I don’t start my morning routine at the exact same time every day, I can still see how long it will take me. If you made these changes it would be lifesaving for me. I usually use Routinist which is perfect for my ADHD, but it doesn’t have an Apple Watch function so I’ve been searching for YEARS for a replacement with the same features but better user interface and Apple Watch capabilities.

If you use any kind of recurring tasks in Apple Reminders, this app will break them repeatedly due to some kind of sync bug. Tasks you've completed will turn up the next day as late, and tasks you haven't done will disappear because Structured has mistakenly set the as completed. This can be downright dangerous if some of your recurring Apple reminders include things like taking medications.

Previous review:
This app kind of feels like a gorgeous Photoshop mockup for an app bit which the actual interface design hasn't been done yet. The layout looks great and intuitive, but the app rarely works the way you'd expect. For example, you can't drag tasks up or down in the timeline, you can't filter types of tasks in the inbox properly, the integration with Apple Reminders doesn't work reliably, . . . etc. If it were a five dollar app, I'd say it was worth buying and holding on to while the developer gradually makes everything work properly, but as a subscription app, it doesn't seem like a wise choice.

body:

No where was this stated in the app, only in the other negative reviews explaining the same scam. 

When you pay for a subscription you should have access to all that comes with. And simply stating it is apples fault does not change the fact that I was charged for this app under false pretences and yet payment was still accepted. So I as the consumer must take the fall by paying for something that was offered to me but can not be fulfilled on your end?  Fix this widget issue or stop advertising as a feature for those who choose to pay for subscriptions.

title: Surprisingly good
body:
When I came across this app I wasn’t expecting much because there are no subscriptions; just a one time payment for the Pro version.  Admittedly, it needs this upgrade to be useful but it is free to try, and if you have a Mac, the measly Pro version price includes the upgrade. Impressive!
I am very happy with this app but I do have a couple of “VERY MINOR”  issues?
1. I have an iPad, iPhone & Mac. If I change a setting (ie selected calendars) on the phone, they do not change on the other devices.
2. The icon color can be changed on the iOS devices but not on the Mac.
3. It would be nice if there was a detailed week/month view option;  currently you can see that there are upcoming events but have to click on the date to see what they are.
Aside from my nitpicking, this is a very nice app well worth the price to get all of the features.

title: GET THE APP NOW
body: I never willingly write reviews but I swear this app is amazing, I had to give my compliments. You can tell the developer truly empathizes with the user and put so much thought into how they wanted the app to function. You don’t have to set the tedious icons, they automatically set to one depending on the task you type. The platform is set to easily access daily, weekly, and monthly views of your schedule. The upgraded feature is only a 1 time payment for a great price. They don’t enforce it on you to pay, you can explore the app before deciding if you want to upgrade. There’s even a fiancé option. I payed for it cause I really believe in this creator and I want to help them make this app even better. The colour options are endless and aesthetically well done. The app syncs to calendar, and it sends you notifications. So if you get distracted by your phone a lot, the app will proactively pull ur attention to your goals. As someone that always resorts to a physical planner and wants to be ego friendly, this app is the key I’ve been looking for. Honestly it’s so well done, I can’t emphasize that enough. Everything you could want as a organizing freak this app has you covered.

title: Efficient and efficient
body:
I was looking for an app to help keep track of my To Do lists and to help actually get them completed. 

This app has filled that need! It syncs w my calendars but also offers up free time periods during which other items can be scheduled. 

There is also a general To-Do list where I can quickly add something and select when I’ll have time to complete it at a later date. If I find I have a gap in my day, I simply refer to this list and add it in to my schedule. 

You can colour code and add icons so for example, I have different colours for work, family, social and self care items or schedules. 

In a short time I have completed things I’ve been meaning to do for months. I’m now going to add a schedule for household maintenance and projects. 

Only suggestion so far would be to have the ability to drag your items to different time slots so if you’re running late you can rearrange your schedule. And a type search for the icons to find the one you want more quickly.

title: 2 Major Issues
body:
In general, this app is pretty good, but there are two major issues I’ve encountered that ruin it. 

1. While the option to copy tasks from a previous day is great, I hate that I put in my schedule for the week, then have to scan through the next month to delete all of the tasks that were randomly repeated. There’s no rhyme or reason to it, it’s just wasting time. 

2. The widget is so frustratingly useless. I have never seen a widget that is so non-functional. You can’t cross off tasks without it opening the app and you can’t scroll through the tasks for the day. It’s basically just a screenshot of the list. My biggest complaint, though, is that it never updates itself. As I’m typing this, the widget hasn’t updating my tasks since 1pm yesterday. In order to have it show the tasks for today, I will have to delete the widget, re-add it to my homepage (it will probably be blank when I do that), then hard restart my phone, maybe a couple times. It’s ridiculous that I have to do this almost every single day. The app is fully updated, so there’s no reason for this.

title: Simple and Functional
body:

As someone who likes to play mobile RPGs casually, it reminds me of the progress bar to reach an objective. I keep my work calendar and personal calendar separate, and this is great for my home routine so I can stop feeling like I’ve lost the entire day.

Room for improvement: 

• CUSTOMIZATION - we choose between a soft pink and black (monochrome). If we’d have other colour options, it would be great. 

• MORE ICONS - love the design, and how we can choose icons for smarter AI. If there’s a happy face, can you add a sad face/neutral face? I know this wasn’t the original purpose, but it would be nice to track my mood. This way, I can identify patterns preventing productivity and when they start.

- An easier way to change the colours of tasks -> ex. using the same selecting feature from the last suggestion and then picking a colour theme for the selected tasks so that you don’t need to do it one by one

- Letting the user choose whatever colour they want for everything to look when using the “Colorful” theme instead of only having the pink option

Great job! :)

title: Bisher die beste App bei ADHS
body:
Bei mir geht es um Fokus und Energiehaushalt (Fatigue). 
Nach einigen Wochen kann ich sagen, dass es für mich keine bessere App gibt. 
Ein paar Wünsche habe ich aber doch:
- Darstellung: proportionale Darstellung der Abstände zwischen den Aufgaben (ev. Logarithmisch, damit der Überblick noch da ist). Bei einem kurzen Blick ist zur Zeit nicht ersichtlich, wie viel Zeit noch zur Verfügung steht. 
- Möglichkeit, eine lange Aufgabe mit Pausen dazwischen zu versehen (z.B. 4h mit 10‘ Pause nach jeder Stunde) mit entsprechender Auswirkung auf die Energiebilanz. Aktuell muss ich dafür 4 Augaben à 50‘ und 4 Pausen à 10‘ eingeben. 
- Synchronisation: Ist Beta und verhält sich so … 3 Geräte, und immer wieder wird eines automatisch abgemeldet. Beim wieder anmelden gehen Änderungen zum Teil verloren bzw. werden durch die älteren Daten überschrieben. 

Vielen Dank!

title: Love it but some limitations can be improved
body:
When two (or more) tasks are scheduled in the same time gap it‘s a mess. Please. Fix this. 

The color palette for tasks is too limited to muted/pastel colors if you want a bright one you must look for the correspondency with web colors and copypaste it. Please put a squared xy color whell instead so we can really choose colors.

Also more background options (color, gradient, pattern or images) would be nice. A schedule is something that you really want to personalize to really relate and be able to engage with. For people with adhd making it personal is the key between love it or leave it. Even fonts to choose would be an easy way to engage.

The possibility to add tasks with no time for a certain date so you can schedule them later even if you already know the date (or dates). They could just be at the end or the beginning of the day waiting to be scheduled or completed. Idk. Sometimes you know that you have to so something today but still don‘t know when exactly.

title: Structured: Technische Probleme mit Benachrichtigungen nach Deinstallation
body:
Nach der Deinstallation von Structured unter macOS wurden weiterhin geplante Benachrichtigungen angezeigt, obwohl die Anwendung nicht mehr installiert war.
Die Herkunft dieser Mitteilungen war zunächst nicht erkennbar. Erst eine technische Untersuchung der macOS-Mitteilungsdatenbank mittels Terminal und SQLite brachte Klarheit:
App-Kennung: com.leomehlig.today (Structured)
29 gespeicherte Benachrichtigungseinträge ohne Zustellzeitpunkt.
Benachrichtigungen erschienen weiterhin nach der ursprünglichen Deinstallation.
Die Bereinigung erforderte eine erneute Installation von Structured und die manuelle Deaktivierung der Mitteilungen sowohl innerhalb der App als auch in den macOS-Systemeinstellungen.
Erst danach waren die 29 Einträge aus der Datenbank verschwunden.
Auch nach erneuter Deinstallation und Neustart blieb die App-Registrierung in der macOS-Datenbank bestehen.
Ob die Ursache in Structured, der Verwaltung geplanter Benachrichtigungen durch macOS oder deren Zusammenspiel liegt, lässt sich nicht abschließend feststellen.
Kritisch ist aus Anwendersicht, dass Benachrichtigungen nach der Deinstallation weiterhin auftraten und zur Behebung technische Eingriffe beziehungsweise eine erneute Installation erforderlich waren.
Von einer Organisations-App erwarte ich, dass geplante Benachrichtigungen zuverlässig verwaltet und beim Entfernen der Anwendung sauber beendet werden.
Fazit: Erheblicher technischer und zeitlicher Aufwand zur Beseitigung unerwünschter Benachrichtigungen. Für mich ein klarer Grund, Structured nicht weiterzuverwenden.

title: Wenig App
body:
Structured. So müsste die App auch aufgebaut sein. Mit Struktur. Mit wenigen Klicks viel erreichen. Als Programmierer hab ich als erstes gelernt, dass Anwendungen ohne viele Klicks bedient werden sollten. Ich öffne das Menü zum bearbeiten einer Aufgabe, nehme keine Änderungen vor und Structured fragt mich, ob ich die Änderungen verwerfen möchte. Welche Änderungen? Ich möchte schnell aus dem Menü, was soll ich hier jetzt noch die nicht vorhandenen Änderungen verwerfen? Statt beim benutzen der App den Usern heimlich zu zeigen und zu leiten wie die App funktioniert, bekommt man ein stumpfes Intro zum durchlesen. Jep. Hab ich mir angeschaut wie jede AGB jemals. Dann befinden sich sinnlose vor definierte Inhalte in der App. Hey. Du stehst um 8 auf und Gehst um 20 ins Bett. Ist doch klar. Wir zeigen aber keine offensichtlichen Optionen wie du diese Aufgaben ändern oder löschen kannst. Nope. Ich kann alle Aufgaben löschen, aber diese beiden nicht. Danke! Der Wecker kommt natürlich noch einmal in eine Extra App. Wäre auch zu schade gewesen, wenn man für 70€ die ganze App bekommen hätte. Nein 50% aufs Abo gibt es, aber nicht auf den dauerhaften Kauf. 

Generell wirkt es eher so als hätten es die Entwickler es nicht geschafft die App richtig aus der Sicht eines neuen Users zu entwickeln. Daher bleiben einige Punkte auf der Strecke und machen die App zu einer App unter vielen. Es ist so, als hat man ne gute Idee gehabt und mittendrin irgendwie das Ziel vor den Augen verloren, weil es zu viele andere Dinge gab auf die man sich konzentrieren wollte. Hier ne Funktion und da ein Feature. Aber nichts richtig bis zu Ende gedacht.

Wieso sind die Widgets so generisch und schlecht? Ineffizienter hätte man den Platz der großen Widgets wirklich nicht mehr nutzen können. Dann hätte man die Großen auch einfach sein lassen können. Die kleinen sind nicht wirklich bedienbar, öffnen halt die App. Wow. 

Wir sprechen von einer App die Nutzende ein Abo oder 70€ kostet.

Dafür hab ich Ansprüche. Auch an eine Fairtrade, bio und vegn hergestellte App aus Deutschland. Aber wir können nicht alle in einem Co-Workingspace in Berlin sitzen und die nächste 0815 App bauen. Es braucht schon etwas Whrgeiz und Willen etwas geiles zu erschaffen.

Es gibt eine Pro-Version mit extra Features, für die es (neben dem Abo) auch ein lebenslänglich-Angebot gibt, was ich sehr ehrenwert finde (mit Abos kriegt man mich nicht).

Da die App für mich in der Praxis super funktioniert und das unter anderem an ihrer Übersichtlichkeit (man wird nicht von vielen kleinen Features erschlagen, die man garnicht verwendet und hat Freiheit sie so zu nutzen, wie es einem am besten passt) und Handhabung (die bisherigen Features sind extrem praktisch) liegt, wünsche ich mir von den Entwicklern einfach nur, dass sich die App in Zukunft nicht grundlegend verändert oder unübersichtlich wird und es weiterhin zumindest immer ein bezahlbares lebenslänglich-Angebot und nicht nur das Abo geben wird.

Good job!

title: Bitte für ADHS optimieren
body:
Ich nutze Structured sehr gerne und finde die App insgesamt wirklich gelungen. Gerade das Design und das Konzept gefallen mir sehr.

Der manuelle Erstellungsprozess von Aufgaben ist für mich allerdings unnötig umständlich. Zuerst muss ich einen Titel eingeben, damit die Vorschläge erscheinen. Danach muss ich auf „Weiter“ klicken. Erst dort kann ich Datum und Uhrzeit festlegen. Möchte ich die Aufgabe ganztägig planen, muss ich zusätzlich noch ein Untermenü öffnen.

Ich würde mir wünschen, dass es ein einziges übersichtliches Fenster gibt, in dem man den Titel, das Datum, die Uhrzeit oder die Option „ganztägig“ direkt festlegen kann. So könnte man eine Aufgabe deutlich schneller und mit weniger Klicks erstellen.

Verbesserungspotenzial sehe ich auch in der Kalenderansicht. Ganztägige Aufgaben werden horizontal nebeneinander dargestellt, wodurch längere Titel schnell abgeschnitten werden. Die Erinnerungen-App von Apple löst das meiner Meinung nach deutlich übersichtlicher. Dort werden Aufgaben untereinander angezeigt, unabhängig davon, ob sie ganztägig sind oder eine feste Uhrzeit haben.

Gerade für neurodivergente Menschen empfinde ich diese Darstellung als deutlich einfacher und intuitiver. Structured ist sehr stark bei der konkreten Planung von Tagen und Uhrzeiten. Es wäre schön, wenn zusätzlich einige der übersichtlichen Listenfunktionen aus Apples Erinnerungen-App übernommen würden.

Außerdem vermisse ich standortbasierte Erinnerungen. Eine Benachrichtigung bei Ankunft oder Abfahrt wäre sehr hilfreich. Auch eine automatische Berechnung der Wegezeit wäre eine tolle Ergänzung.

Insgesamt ist Structured eine sehr gute App mit viel Potenzial. Mit einem einfacheren Erstellungsprozess, einer übersichtlicheren Darstellung ganztägiger Aufgaben sowie Funktionen wie Geofencing und Wegezeit wäre sie für mich nahezu perfekt.

title: LieblingsApp
body:
Structured-Power to the People

Ich- mit ADHS im Moment so am Strugglen, dass sich mein Gehirn anfühlt wie ein Sieb, habe schon viele Systeme ausprobiert, oft überfordernde.

Zugegeben, jedes System bedarf einer Einarbeitungszeit, und ich denke, ich musste insbesondere erst einmal verstehen, was bei mir gut oder weniger gut funktioniert.ich bin froh das ich auf Structured gestoßen bin. 

Für mich ist Structured da nach tieferem Blick mit seiner puristischen, schnörkellosen Aufmachung schon nach kurzer Zeit zu einer Wohltat für mein Puddinghirn geworden. Die Energie, die vorher für die Verwaltung von zahllosen Apps und Zettelsystemen unwiederbringlich im Äther verpuffte, zahlt sich jetzt tatsächlich auf Dinge jenseits vom Planungsirrsinn aus.

Wer sich kurz ein kleines bisschen spielerisch mit Structured auseinandersetzt, dazu die Erinnerungen und den Kalender von Apple nutzt, der darf sich das schnelle und reibungslose Erfassen von Aufgaben und Ereignissen auf der Fontanelle zergehen lassen.

Ich vermeide damit langes Vorplanen über lange Zeit, und keine App kann den Faktor Mensch komplett obsolet machen. Gut, dass Structureds strukturierte Struktur nicht destrukturierbar ist. Denn viele gut durchdachte Dinge von Structured leuchten einem nach und nach ein, und man kann froh sein, dass man sie nicht ändern konnte.

Ich so:
	•	Als Erstes Structured auf – klare Timeline mit den Apple-Erinnerungen und Kalendereinträgen. Jetzt weiß ich, welche Verpflichtungen anliegen.
	•	Morgens ohne Ablenkung, per Sprache formulierend, die KI zwingen, für mich die Aufgaben in Form zu bringen. Diese erscheinen dann sofort in der App (der Fokus bleibt bei mir). Aufgaben vom Vortag swipe ich nach automatischer Erinnerung spielerisch mit lockerem Handgelenk. Ich kann dem System vertrauen und muss keine Angst haben, dass ich Wichtiges verkacke.
	•	Alles, was so über den Tag verteilt von außen meiner Aufmerksamkeit bedarf, spreche ich als Erinnerung in meine Apple Watch ein. Dies landet dann auch automatisch in der Timeline. Kein Papierkram. Keine Verzögerung. Kein nachher Suchen müssen.
	•	Ich kann sogar mit meiner VR-Brille Bürokram über den Browser machen, da sowohl die Apps wie Erinnerungen und Kalender als auch Structured über den Browser durch Synchronisation mit dem Gerät der Wahl, den Bedürfnissen angepasst, bedienbar sind.

Ich hätte noch einige Methoden zum Thema Zeitmanagement, Workflows und individuell anpassbaren, bevorzugten Arbeitsweisen, die bestimmt schon viele mit ADHS bewusst oder unbewusst ansprechen bzw. weitergeholfen haben.

Ich hätte so Lust, mal mit dem Entwickler im Austausch zu stehen und mich mit ihm über seine Gedanken auszutauschen.

An dieser Stelle aber möchte ich die längste Rezension der Welt zu einem Ende kommen lassen und mich herzlich bei den Menschen bedanken, die diese App hier ins Leben gerufen haben, in dem Bewusstsein, dass bereits schon lange ein wirklich nutzerfreundliches, ohne sich mit Abos aufdrängendes und an den Verbraucher angepasstes Hilfsmittel für immer einen Platz in meinem Herzen gefunden hat.
author: Flow&Structure

title: ADHD’s best friend!
body:
I’ve tried so many planning and productivity apps over the years, and Structured is hands down the best one so far.

For just 15€ a year, the value is incredible. It has everything I need to actually function with ADHD instead of constantly fighting against it. It helps me organize my tasks and sub-tasks, reschedule them easily when life happens, and build a fixed routine, which is absolutely essential for ADHD brains.

For the first time ever, I’ve been able to maintain and develop habits, thanks to the reminders and dynamic scheduling. The app is flexible without being chaotic, which is such a rare balance. The user-friendly colorful interface also makes it exciting!

One of my favorite features is how seamlessly it syncs with my reminders, calendar, and Outlook, combining my private and work to-do lists. Everything lives in one place, which removes so much mental clutter. Not to mention AI integration for planning my day for me when I feel overwhelmed!

The Apple Watch app is a game changer. Having reminders right on my wrist means I don’t forget tasks anymore, and if I do forget to finish something, Structured gently reminds me without guilt or pressure.

As someone with ADHD, I really appreciate how the app accounts for energy levels. It helped me let go of the shame around procrastination by showing that some tasks simply require more energy and that it’s okay to pause, reschedule, and come back later.

It’s also amazing for women: by connecting with Apple Health and menstrual cycle data, it helps you understand when it’s a good time to plan high-energy tasks versus when it’s better to slow down and rest. That insight alone is priceless.

Structured is a life-changer. Thank you so much to the developers, you’ve built something truly special. 💛

title: Super App mit Luft nach oben (Pro Version)
body:
Ich liebe die App, aber einige Punkte stören mich noch:

1. Einstellung der Dauer einer Aufgabe
Hier hat man eine Limitierung von 6 Zeitangaben (z.B. 30min, 1h, 1:30h usw.) 
Dadurch muss ich oft in die manuelle Eingabe geben, die aber manchmal echt schwierig ist zu bedienen, vor allem wenn man mit einer Aufgabe über die Mitternacht rutscht wird es kniffelig. 

2. Ganztätige Aufgabe
Warum gibt es hier nicht einfach eine Checkbox direkt neben der Zeiteinstellung? 
Man muss erstmal auf die drei Punkte klicken, um eine ganztägige Aufgabe anzulegen. Im Alltag echt nervig, kommt auch wirklich oft vor.

3. Kategorien anlegen 
Es wäre toll, wenn man die Möglichkeit hätte, Kategorien zu definieren. Z.B. „Arbeit“, „Einkaufen“ „Haushalt“ usw. denen man dann Farben zuordnen kann. Das ist aber kein Musst Have, nur ein Nice to Have. 

Ansonsten liebe ich das Interface der App und bin ein großer Fan von den Unteraufgaben. Ich habe die App mittlerweile als Widget auf meinem Macbook und kann damit meinen Alltag richtig gut planen.

title: Ohne Upgrade lohnt es sich nicht

Wer die App noch nicht hat versteht das jetzt vermutlich nicht, aber ich würde sagen, dass die App ohne Upgrade mehr zu Zeitverschwendung führt und nicht dazu, dass man die Zeit effizienter nutzt. Mit Upgrade würde ich sie aber wirklich empfehlen, deshalb den einen Stern. Den anderen Stern habe ich gegeben, da man auch ohne Upgrade sehen kann in welcher Phase der Periode man sich gerade befindet (Lutealphase,…) und man auch sehen kann wann man sich dann oft am produktivsten fühlt. Das geht aber nur wenn man auf apple Health seine Periode trackt (glaube ich)

title: a blessing for my adhd time blindness
body:
The way this app visualizes time frames — and the fact that Structured can sync with my calendar — has honestly been a blessing for my very questionable sense of time. Whenever I have an important day coming up, I map out all my appointments, tasks, steps, and how long each one will take. I’ve never been this punctual in my life, lol.
The simple interface and the fact that recurring tasks appear as templates make it easier to stick with the app, which is impressive given how easily I usually lose track of tools like this.

title: Seit Update nicht mehr zufrieden
body:

Auch finde ich es nicht so optimal das die Leiste nach unten gewandert ist. Vorher war perfekt. Kalender, Inbox alles in einer Reihe. So finde ich die Bedienung eher als Rückschritt.
Es ist nicht mehr ersichtlich wie mal jetzt sich wiederholende Termine eingeben soll. 
Leider wieder für dieses Jahr bezahlt. Die App ist so unbrauchbar und nicht mehr so einfach zu bedienen wie vorher.
Update Oktober2025: App hängt sich reproduzierbar komplett auf wenn man einen Termin im Kalender 2026 öffnen will. 
Ganz ehrlich, die App wurde verschlimmbessert.
Dezember 2025:
Es wäre schön, wenn man in der iPad App mal Termine in den Wochen verschieben könnte ohne das da immer der Rand verschwindet. Das ist so nicht nutzbar und nervig da man so jedesmal in jeden Termin reingehen muss und den Termin von Hand ändern. Statt am Interface und der Optik bitte endlich mal an der Bedienung arbeiten. Das war mal besser.

title: Old version was better!
body:
Hey, at first I’d like to say that I used to really love this app. But since the old update, before the current, it’s now nearly impossible to choose a nice color, it’s only possible if you copy paste the colors from old tasks into the new one. I think it’s not okay to only make that possible if you pay for the pro version! Of course the pro version users should get some bonuses, but don’t take what’s left for those who don’t pay!
The current update made it so much more uncomfortable to add a task. I have to go through so many different sites to add color, to choose the time, to write down notes. You made it very complicated, it’s consuming too much time and effort now. And if the task is too long (like 3 words “too much”) the end will be just chopped off and not possible to see (except if you type on that task and swipe until the end of the sentence).

title: Schedule doesn‘t adapt
body:
The app is really cute and seems incredibly useful and practical at first, but the problem quickly starts as soon as you run a bit late. You‘d think that if you schedule something five minutes later than originally , every other task would also begin five minutes later, or it would at least give you the option to make every other task five minutes later as well. Instead, you have to reschedule every single task on your own, every single time, I you don‘t want your tasks overlapping. It turns a tool that was supposed to help you establish a peaceful routine into something super stressful, because if you run late for a task, you have to manually change the starting time for every other task, and that takes time.
And if that’s a premium feature, then that’s kinda whack.

title: You'll lose all your data – Don't switch from iCloud to Structured Cloud
body:
The Structured app seems to be completely defective, as the “Wake up” reminder has entered itself automatically over 400 times within 24 hours – per day.
And the number keeps growing.

This happened as soon as I switched from iCloud to Structured Cloud.

What is the point of this app if such a bug occurs?!

Structured shows that this app is completely unreliable and that the developers obviously don't know what they are doing.

The recommendation from the service:
- Take a previous backup from iCloud.
- Delete all entries completely.

There is no backup in my iCloud because I trusted Structured and switched to their obviously useless cloud.

Having to completely reset the app is madness, as this will result in the loss of all entries.

And going back to the last backup is not a solution.
How often are we supposed to put up with this nonsense when it's now clear that this problem could happen again and again because Structured doesn't know what they're doing.

It's probably better to delete the entire app right away.

No one needs poor development and unreliable apps.

A to-do app is supposed to keep things organized and save time.

So far, the Structured app has only caused a lot of frustration and wasted time!!!

title: Gut bei ADHS, auf dem Mac nicht barrierefrei Die App selbst ist für Menschen, die ADHS haben und Hil
body:
Die App selbst ist für Menschen, die ADHS haben und Hilfe bei der Tagesstruktur benötigen wirklich toll. Sie ist einfach zu bedienen und die KI Features helfen extrem gut, bei der Tagesplanung. Auch die Einfachheit deer Eintragserstellung und die Kalender- und Erinnerungsverknüpfungen sind alle wirklich durchdacht und einfach zu nutzen.

Auf dem iPhone ist die App wirklich toll für blinde zu bedienen. Es gibt keine plötzlichen Fokussprünge, die Buttons, slider und sonstige Menüs sind allesamt gut beschriftet und mit dem eingebauten Screenreader gut zu nutzen.

Auf dem Mac jedoch gibt es deutliche Probleme für blinde Nutzer. 
Der Fokus springt immer wieder vom gewählten Element weg, die App ist kathastrofal auf dem Mac für blinde mit dem Screenreder zu bedienen. Ich kann nichts vernünftig einstellen, da ich fast keinen Punkt einfach erreichen kann und der Fokus immer wieder weg gezogen wird, zum ersten Eintrag des Fensters, der meist der „schließen“ Button ist. 
Ich bitte Sie, das Entwicklungsteam, hier deutlich und bitte so schnell wie möglich, nachzulegen. Ich möchte die App wirklich gerne nutzen und sie auch weiter empfehlen, aber mit den Barrierefreiheits-Einbußen ist es auf dem Mac einfach nicht möglich.

title: Gute App aber manchmal Verwirrent
body:
Die App ist grundsätzlich hilfreich zur Tagesplanung, hat aber einige Schwächen:
	•	Heutiger Tag wird nicht hervorgehoben: Es wäre sinnvoll, wenn der aktuelle Tag deutlich markiert wäre, z. B. mit einem grauen Kreis. Aktuell fehlt diese visuelle Orientierung komplett.
	•	AI versteht Wochentage nicht richtig: Wenn man der AI z. B. sagt, „Termin am Montag“, wird dieser auf den letzten Montag statt auf den nächsten gelegt. Das führt zu Fehlern bei der Planung.
	•	Widgets unklar dargestellt: In den Widgets fehlen die Tagesangaben. Bei mehreren Terminen an verschiedenen Tagen sieht man nur die Uhrzeit, was verwirrend ist. Ein klarer Hinweis auf den jeweiligen Tag wäre hier wichtig.

Insgesamt gute Ansätze, aber Verbesserungsbedarf bei der Benutzerführung und Logik.

title: eine große Hilfe im Alltag
body:
als neurodivergente Person suchte ich flexible Planung meines Alltags, bei der die Zeiten visuell gut für mich ersichtlich sind. Das hat Structured auf jeden Fall geschafft! Ein weiteres Feature, das mir letztens erst aufgefallen ist: Ich kann einstellen, dass ich pro Tag ein Energiepensum eintragen kann, sowie den Aufgaben den Energieaufwand zuweisen kann. Das ist eine enorme Hilfe bei meinem derzeitigen Plan, mit der wenigen Energie, die ich als „Spoonie“ habe, meinen Alltag zu strukturieren. Großes Lob dafür!
Was ich mir jedoch wünsche ist, dass ich einen Katalog an Aufgaben erstellen kann mit Aufgaben, die sich in meinem Alltag häufig wiederholen - und aus dem ich die fertig erstellten Aufgaben jeweils einfach in mein Kalenderfeld ziehen kann. Ich möchte nicht nur die vorher genutzten Aufgaben, die mir ein Eingeben vorgeschlagen werden, nutzen, sondern hätte gerne eine Blaupause für diese feststehenden Aufgaben. Denn oft gibt es kleine Änderungen z.B. an der Dauer, die ich aber nur für einen bestimmten Tag ändern möchte. Wenn diese Änderung bei den folgenden Malen jedes Mal vorgeschlagen wird und ich nicht auf eine ursprüngliche Blaupause  zugreifen kann, ist das lästig. Sollte es bald solch einen Aufgabenkatalog geben, wäre ich sehr glücklich! Alles in allem aber eine wirklich sehr gute App, die auf die Bedürfnisse von Menschen mit ADHS, Autismus und chronischen Erkrankungen zugeschniten ist. Danke!
