title: Super app mais il faut posséder les derniers modèles d’iPhone
body:
Grâce à cette app vous pouvez centraliser votre calendrier et vos rappels dans un seul endroit. Ce qui fait que si vous savez vous servir de votre calendrier et de vos rappels correctement, vous pourrez faire du timeblocking avec cette app, maîtriser, optimiser votre temps et ne plus en perdre. Vous pouvez créer des tâches avec sous-tâches ou notes, récurrentes ou pas, choisir les jours de là semaines de cette tâche, etc. Les possibilités sont très grandes. Les moins. Le développeur n’est pas joignable. L’appli freeze en multitâche, a du mal à se synchroniser surtout avec rappel et fait chauffer votre iPhone. C’était le cas pour moi qui avait l’iPhone 11 Pro mais dès que je suis passer au 14 pro, la plupart des problèmes ce sont réglés sauf l’app qui fait toujours beaucoup chauffer l’iPhone.

Ce qui serait super aussi c’est de pouvoir créer une zone de temps : par exemple une zone de travail de 9h à 12h et de pouvoir y créer d’autres tâches dans cette zone comme des réunions avec leur heure de début, leur durées, leur tâches secondaires, etc; au lieu d’avoir un visuel où les tâches se chevauchent.

title: Prometteur mais améliorable
body: Le concept de l’app est vraiment super. C’est utile au quotidien pour améliorer la visualisation et la gestion de son temps, surtout quand on a des difficultés à garder son attention et à se repérer dans la temporalité. Pour moi ça remplit vraiment un besoin, merci. Pourtant, à mon sens, il manque encore des fonctionnalités à l’appli pour être gagner en simplicité d’utilisation et devenir vraiment ergonomique : - pouvoir modifier les tâches en swippant, sans a voir à cliquer sur un bouton, puis un autre, puis encore un autre… Ce qui prend du temps et qui est laborieux. - pouvoir sélectionner plusieurs tâches à la fois (pour les supprimer ou les déplacer). - Et surtout, pouvoir modifier l’enchainement des tâches sur la ligne verticale, juste en appuyant dessus et en les faisant glisser directement au dessus ou en dessous des autres, sans avoir à cliquer sur la tache, ouvrir le panneau de notification et changer son créneau horaire manuellement. Je crois les doigts pour que ces remarques attirent l’attention des développeurs et des développeuses ! Merci pour le travail déjà engagé.

title: Nice structure and modules... to improve maybe!
body:
I enjoy the layout, the structure (timeline, subtasks and notes, recurring events, calendar sync) and the aesthetics.
However, some things could be improved in my opinion.
It is a bit time consuming to change the timing of a task (calendar from the apple appstore is much easier in that regard: you can drag the task along the timeline). Similarly, I would like to toggle subastsks (the ones you have to tick) because I usually do subtasks in a certain order, especially recurring tasks, and when you add new subtasks you cannot change easily the order. Plus the subtasks could disappear or fade when completer. I really enjoy these features in the MinimaList app for instance. Basically: drag and drop, toggle from one place to another, removing completed tasks would considerably improve the UX in my opinion. Also, a view of the tasks in a weekly layout would be great!

title: Presque parfait 🙂
body:
J’aime beaucoup l’application aussi j’ai rapidement pris la version payante sans hésiter. J’ai un trouble de l’attention et une application aidant à structurer sa journée devient indispensable. Je n’ai malheureusement pas encore trouvé à ce jour celle qui est parfaite, mais Structured s’en approche. 
 Pour moi il manquerait : 

 - la possibilité de ajouter une liste à cocher ou des notes dans les tâches. Et lorsque cette tâche est récurrente, que la liste dans la tâche se renouvelle à chaque fois. Par exemple si je coche un élément de la liste le lundi, il faut que cet élément ne se coche pas automatiquement sur toute la série, je dois pouvoir la cocher quotidiennement. Cela permettrait d’inclure des routines avec une liste de choses à faire. 
 - Pour les récurrences aussi, permettre de sélectionner : 1 semaine sur 2, ou sur 3, serait aussi très bien. 
 - la possibilité de personnaliser les notifications (son et texte) 
- la possibilité de mettre une date de fin à une tâche 

Je ne m’inquiète pas, je sais que l’application est jeune et l’initiative est super. Bravo au développeur !

title: Important features missing
body:
I thought I had finally found my perfect task management app, but sadly not.  

Unfortunately there is no facility to allocate a priority to tasks.  A key part of time management is capturing the tasks that need doing and being able to prioritise them BEFORE you schedule them in your day.  This app jumps straight into scheduling without giving a system for choosing which tasks are actually needed.   In an ideal world you should be able to set up a system for how you prioritise your tasks (there are a variety of different ways), and view your tasks in a priority view THEN schedule. Apps like tick tick or todoist do this very well but don’t have the visual appeal of Structured.  I would totally switch if the task capturing and prioritisation side of Structured was improved.

title: Good concept, but persistent freezing makes it unreliable
body:
I'm a paying annual subscriber and genuinely like what Structured is trying to do. The timeline view is thoughtful and the sync across devices works well, when the app is actually running.

The problem is that on macOS the app freezes regularly and stops responding entirely. The only fix is a Force Quit. This has happened often enough that I no longer trust the app to be open when I need it. For a daily planner, that's a serious reliability issue.

I'd also encourage the developer to revisit what data is being sent to third-party services:
posthog.com
8-lives-cat.io
revenuecat.com
configcat.com
sentry.io

As a paying customer I was surprised to find the app contacts analytics platforms in the background,the kind of behavioural tracking that makes sense for a free app trying to convert users, less so for an annual subscription.

I want to keep using Structured. But the freezing needs to be fixed, and paying users deserve transparency about what the app is doing in the background.

title: Good but needs something else to make it stand out even more
body:
I keep coming back to this app but sometimes there is something it still needs to keep me using it…

The app has strong structure and works well for organising both work and personal routines, but it falls short when it comes to flexibility and personalisation. Managing recurring tasks is straightforward on a weekly basis, however it becomes inefficient when routines vary, such as alternating days off or changes in schedule. A key improvement would be the introduction of “template days” or “day types” (e.g. workday, day off, holiday, event day) that can be applied to any date, allowing tasks to adjust automatically without constant manual editing. In addition, notification options are limited—there should be the ability to add audio to tasks or customise notification sounds so important reminders stand out and are not missed. It would also be beneficial to have a clearer, dedicated notes area separated from tasks, allowing users to capture information, thoughts, or context without cluttering actionable items. These improvements would significantly reduce friction, improve consistency, and make the system far more practical for real-life use where schedules and priorities constantly shift.

title: Love the app, but the event time selector is a nightmare
body:
The Structured app has garnered considerable admiration for its aesthetic design and overall utility. However, there exists a particular feature that has proven to be quite frustrating: the process of setting start and end times for events.

The time selector, it appears, is unnecessarily complicated and lacks user-friendliness. A minor error can result in a tedious correction process that may take anywhere from 20 to 30 minutes. Moreover, adjusting the start time often inadvertently alters the end time, creating a cumbersome cycle of adjustments that can be exasperating.

Additionally, the options for jumping ahead by+1 and +2 hours seem to introduce more confusion than clarity. It would be beneficial for the Structured team to consider simplifying the time selection process. Despite the app's many strengths, enhancing this particular feature could significantly improve user experience, allowing individuals to manage their schedules more efficiently. After all, time is a precious resource, and users should not have to expend excessive effort merely to organize it.

title: A Masterclass in Daily Planning
body:
Structuring my day has never been easier.

Structured takes the chaos of a full schedule and turns it into something that feels calm, clear, and completely manageable. The app strikes the perfect balance between functionality and elegance. It doesn’t just look good—it feels good to use. Every detail, from the subtle haptics to the colour choices and smooth animations, is clearly built to mirror Apple’s design aesthetic. It feels like something Apple could’ve made themselves—seamless, intuitive, and genuinely native.

The timeline-based layout is a game changer. Unlike traditional calendar or to-do apps, Structured gives your day a clear flow, which makes staying on track almost effortless. The interface is so well thought out that it practically encourages productivity without ever feeling overwhelming.

From quick task creation with natural language to its satisfying checkmarks and widgets that keep you grounded throughout the day, Structured nails every touchpoint. Syncing across devices works flawlessly, and with support for Siri and Shortcuts, it integrates beautifully into my daily routine.

If you’ve been struggling to manage your time, or just want an app that genuinely helps you enjoy planning, Structured is a must-have. It’s not just another productivity app—it’s the app I now rely on to give shape to my day.

title: Great app - worst AI I’ve encountered
body:
The app itself is fantastic. It provides a lot of flexibility and makes scheduling better in general. I love being able to choose icons and colours to be able to categorise. There is a large selection and you can see they’ve put a lot of work into it.

There are a few very clunky parts though, trying to change the time requires going through multiple menus, as do a few options. It makes everything take a lot longer. There are just too many things to click through which imo could be accomplished with a single window and not having to close 3 windows every time you make a change.

As for the AI - it might be called AI but I’ve met more intelligent 2 year olds. Basic functionality like replicating days is almost impossible. This leaves you having to completely design the same day multiple times - unless you’re ready to set everything up as a repeating task, but when is that ever a reality? If the AI cannot replicate a day in a scheduler then how much use is it really? Ask it to move something, it will screw it up. Ask it to help with any of the features that you get with the paid subscription and you will want to throw your pc out of the window. It requires a LOT of work and is nowhere near being helpful in any way.

That being said, I would, despite all of it’s shortcomings still pay for it again, as using it without the paid options isn’t quite the same.

If you don’t want to use generative AI for privacy, ethical or environmental reasons the tab will always be there. I think the best way to balance the people who have no interest in the AI features and the ones who find it really useful is to make the AI tab optional. Add an option in the settings to choose whether you want that tab visible or not. I think it’s the best approach in world where every tech corporation is shoving AI in your face and begging you to use it. This also would align better with the app’s focus on privacy too. I have lifetime premium so I’ll continue to use this app for the daily planner purposes I downloaded it for and it’s good at that I just think there could be a better compromise with the AI.

title: Great for neurodivergence/fatigue
body:
I have ADHD and fatigue from long Covid. The ability to track the energy that tasks drain and set an energy budget for each day is unique to Structured, I think, and over the last few days it's been helping me turn my life around (and that's not ADHD exaggeration!). What's really helped is the recognition that, with ADHD, if I don't set aside specific time for a task, then I'm unlikely to be able to do it. So Structured has started to feel like critical assistive technology for me.

It's close to perfect. Even though it doesn't have full calendar integration, it makes it very easy to edit Apple Calendar events through a modal, so no problems with that. I've given it 4/5 rather than 5/5 for these things which I hope will be improved:

• I can't adjust the length of events with touch-drag, only their start-time. There needs to be the ability to long-press near the end of an event bar to adjust its time.
• I'd like a settings option to say that when I'm touch-dragging events around, the adjustment will snap to increments of 5 minutes (or 15 mintes, or 1 minute (for the weirdos who like to set events with 1-minute accuracy!)).
• For a task system, there needs to be additional categories than just "Inbox" in which to store tasks, eg with "folders" or similar. Without this, I need to keep using an external tool to track tasks for projects, then copy them into Structured in some way when they need to get done.

The overly-precise event dragging and lack of drag/drop event length I decided I could live with.

The lack of task folders for non-scheduled tasks means I need an external tool for my projects (I'm using Obsidian, but Todoist is great too), but Structured's time-line and energy tracking has such value that it's worth it for me to have an extra app in my process. Also, in honesty, the limitation of having only an inbox for non-scheduled tasks is interesting in a positive way. It's helping me to not overthink day-to-day planning, because overthinking/overcomplexity is a mostly harmful tedency I have. So when Structured implements task folders (which I hope they do), I'll try to keep hold of what this limitation is teaching me and not overcomplicate my folders and bury things.

Definitely recommend you take a look if you have fatigue/pacing challenges. I think it's fantastic value, especially on a yearly plan.

title: There is room for improvement
body:
Only a few things in things in this app frustrate me. If there were more I’d comment on them, but overal it’s great.

Here are some suggestions for the current version in the order of priority:

- Add buffer time: events and tasks can be scheduled with the travel/buffer time attached to the main task or event. Why a lack of it is a problem: 1) without the buffer time, total amount of time I need to get to the task is not factored in; 2) if I add the travel time by including it into the main task, then the app will count it as one long task and deduct incorrect amount of energy required to complete it.

- Add the ability to set and adjust time by manually typing it on the keypad. The current way to enter the time is logical, but also makes the time-setting unnecessarily complicated. There is simply too much on the screen, especially when compared to how other calendar apps do this. There should be at least an option to type in the time manually to let people avoid all the scrolling hustle.

- Add custom notification sounds (the ones that can be uploaded in iCloud or OneDrive).

- More convenient & quick way to reschedule events by moving them between days: by adding a monthly or weekly view and allowing to drag an item from one day to another.

I looked this issue up in the app’s FAQ section and it’s on the creator’s ‘to do’ list but it’s been there for two years….how long do users have to wait for this priority feature? Many users have fed back there that it’s stopping them committing to Structured, preventing them from leaving other similar apps.

title: Perfect planning
body:
As an avid user of a Bullet Journal, this type of day by day planning is perfect for me. The problem I always had with physical journaling was that I may not always have the book with me and altering tasks and events time and can become messy.

Structured is essentially the same format but with a daily timeline in place. I put a load of tasks in the inbox and transfer them to my day when I feel like completing them. It’s an excellent way of decluttering your mind and focussing on what you need to do now. The interface is extremely user friendly and I honestly couldn’t ask it to be better at what it does.

If I could ask for anything it would be to implement longer term planning. For myself I start with what I want for the year, then create tasks for the month based on what needs to be achieved. Those monthly tasks are essentially my inbox in Structured but it would be amazing to have an overview of how some smaller activities add up to complete larger objectives. Any thoughts from the developers here would be appreciated. Keep up the great work guys!!

Structured not only provides a clear vertical timeline for displaying tasks but also tracks and measures my daily energy, making my capability limits clear. This helps me avoid setting daily goals that are too high, which could damage my limited self-confidence and self-discipline. Additionally, one of my favorite features is its ability to integrate with calendars and reminders. Whenever changes occur in the other two apps, Structured quickly synchronizes, which is very convenient for managing multiple long-term plans. Last but not least, Structured offers a one-year scholarship and even full scholarships for students with financial constraints, which is truly amazing! I am very grateful to Structured for providing such a great opportunity to become more efficient and confident.

body:

Did I mention that the timeline also clearly tells you the amount of free time between tasks? It’s really good!  Also the widget keeps a running timeline in real time, so you can see how long your current task has left, and what is coming up next?

All in all a good app for those of us who work well with a clear list and reminders, but want something that isn’t too overwhelming to set up. I have ADHD and the difference this app has made is astounding.  I did the free trial and then happily slid into the paid subscription, which is incredibly reasonably priced.

Thanks Structured, you are amazing!

title: genuinely life changing
body:
i never usually review anything! especially apps. but oh my goodness.

i’m a university student with pretty severe ADD and depression. i get really terrible ADD paralysis, meaning no matter how much i want or need to do something, i physically can’t move / get up to do it. I have nearly failed my course, which I only passed by working for a week straight, almost 15 hours most days. this completely shattered me. 

What i’m saying is that i find it almost impossible to do anything if i’m not under panic attack-inducing pressure. 

This changed when I started using this app again. i started on the standard version about a year ago which i loved so much that I decided to upgrade to premium. after applying for a discounted rate (due to my circumstances) i was able to pay significantly less which has also helped me hugely (THANK YOU SO MUCH!). I now feel motivated to get things done without having to fight the ‘just do it later’ voice in my head. i’ve got so much done without getting too stressed, and most importantly i’ve learnt the ways I work the most productively in. the app helps you to realistically plan your day with the ‘energy limit’ which helps you track how much energy each task gives or takes, and how much energy you have to spare each day. 

I have some suggestions that would make this app perfect! When a task takes longer than planned, i find myself having to individually adjust the rest of the tasks in the day. If i could move all incomplete tasks forward an hour at once, for example, this would save a huge amount of time. 

I love the AI feature, but I would like to be able to adjust the timings of each task before i add them to my day. 

The last thing - the energy limit feature would work so much better if i had more options (e.g. some tasks are more energy restoring than others, and would also like more than 3 ⚡️options). 

Thank you again to the developers behind this app!❤️

title: Lovely app which works in synergy with existing to do lists
body: Ok, so I’m a to do list nerd. This helps with adhd and time impermenace and is almost a hybrid calendar / to do. My workflow using it is putting in the silly little things I do through a day - bath coffee etc - and then blocking time for bigger stints such as write key emails. It means v easily you can cross ref the day and see if you’re ahead / behind. So stops the constant adhd angst that you’ve forgotten to do something or need to be doing something else. For me that is particularly bad if I have a flight / zoom / theatre in the evening and I easily lose track. Or panic about getting ready 4 hours out. I’m writing this in the bath, safe in the knowledge I’ve got another 15 mins allocated before the day moves on. I don’t use it as main to do list I just tend to port some time sensitive stuff over to it and tick it off. The ai Planner works very well to propagate the day. And it’s great if you’ve lost a morning to pull back some structure to the day. Strong recommend and I’ve tried every single app that’s similar. OmniFocus and this, and recently one sec which they recommend on structured.

title: Works for me
body:
I’m really enjoying this app so far. It seems to work for me and the way I think about tasks. I like the way I don’t have to plan everything out right away, I can throw tasks into the inbox as I think of them and then plan when to do them when I’m ready. Personally I prefer to do that close to the time, so I can look at the planner for the next day, see the gaps and put tasks in there. I like that the app is still in development and look forward to new features. 

Speaking of, I’m not sure of the best way to suggest new features (maybe a new feature could be a suggestions box?) but I’d like it to be easier to get tasks into the planner from the inbox. Drag and drop is quite clunky on an iPhone. When I tap the little + button in a gap in the planner it brings up an add task dialog which has some suggested tasks but those are set by the system I think and nothing to do with me. It would be good if those suggested tasks could be inbox tasks. 

Even better would be if it could look at your gaps across the next week and suggest where you could fit in your inbox tasks. And, even more gold plated, if there was a weather feature so you could tell it whether a task is indoor or outdoor and it would know not to suggest outdoor tasks when there is bad weather forecast. 

But, overall this is a fantastic app and really helped me, a not very organised or productive person, get organised and productive. The pricing is also fantastic for what you get and I’m grateful to the devs for making it so affordable.

title: Easily beats every other app
body:
I have spent years trying to get other to do list and time tracking apps working for my ADHD. Structured wins, hands down, no contest. Not only does it make you think of tasks in terms of time - including when you move something from your inbox to a set date - but it also doesn’t punish you for missing days.

You won’t wake up after two days off to a wall of missed tasks; just a clean slate you can start adding the things you missed to yourself. It’s helped me so much with my morning routine, with my planning on my WFH days and with using my days more effectively. I can’t recommend Structured enough to anyone who uses a to do list app well for a month or two and then it all falls apart after a mild disruption.

Really can’t stress enough what a great job the Structured team have done at what for this day and age is an incredibly reasonable price. This is what great productivity apps should be: simple, elegant, purpose-driven, and cost-effective.

I’d also like to add that this little app got me all the way through my uni degree and helped me get a first. I’m sure that without Structured taking away some of the day-to-day cognitive overhead of dealing with life in general, I wouldn’t have achieved my goal. 

Thank you, Leo, from the bottom of my heart, for making such a life-changing application.

title: New Favourite App
body:
I have tried many apps in the store, from Apple’s; Reminders, to the overpriced ‘Productivity’, but I still fell behind running my own business.
Structured has the daily tasks you set, but where it’s unique is in 3 areas:
1/. The integration with your daily iCalander appointments, and Reminders app is just so well thought out. This means you can see what you can realistically achieve, what needs delegated, and what needs carried to tomorrow.
2/. The app window on Mac is a perfect size to keep open & visible, so you can see how long you have been working on your subject, and how long you have left.
3/. With the One Sec App integration, it just makes you think for a moment, before you waste 5 minutes on social media (which always ends up being 45 minutes), which again is an excellent feature.
In top of all this, they are not charging a rip-off price, which is why so many are happy to give 5 Star reviews. Everyone is entitled to make a profit, but we all know the difference when we are being taken for a ride.
So, in short, this app is my new favourite app and on my iPhone, Apple Watch & iPad Home Screen. It definitely makes me more productive, which makes me more money, makes me feel more motivated, I can see what I have achieved, and when I am finished, and with my family, I am not sneaking to do some work anymore.
Thank you for a simple, but very effective app!🙏

title: Nice concept, but unusably buggy
body:
I love the idea of stringing together a schedule for my working week, visually. This app shows all the signs of being good at doing that, but is let down my some pretty fundamental bugs. 

- Syncing with Apple Calendar forces the app to crash on both iPadOS and iOS
- Syncing between iPhone and iPad is incorrect
- I had issues using my premium subscription on my iPhone, after signing up on my iPad.

Also, I’m not an avid user of the Reminders app - it would be nice to integrate with something like Todoist, or another third party task manager.

The dev really needs to figure out what's going on here as I can't rely on it at this point.  As far as I can tell, it sporadically happens when a process called 'keychain (structured) appears.

I'll update my review if this is fixed, but currently I can't recommend it.

title: So far, so great!
body:

I decided to give Structured a try and so far it’s working out great! I really like the easy to understand design and how it’s laid out to help me quickly refer back to what I need to do during the day, even if that’s remembering to drink or make myself something to eat. I love to use it at the weekend too, and I really enjoy forward planning and thinking ‘what can I achieve this weekend?’ rather than wasting it zoning out on yet another box set.

Just two tiny things I’ve noticed so far. There’s two typos on the icon selection page: it should be ‘Clothes’ not ‘Cloths’ and ‘Food and Drinks’ is usually written as ‘Food and Drink’.

title: Amazing for those with ADHD
body:
This is such a helpful, pretty app! It was recommended to me by my mentor, and as a uni student with ADHD it has been a Godsend!! 

Planning is easy, and very visual- which really helps if like me, words and numbers don’t mean a lot. I need to see time passing, and see chunks of my day blocked out, otherwise I’m totally time blind. That’s what makes this app stand out from other dairies. 

Also I love the colour and emoticon choices, its so aesthetic and makes planning my day so pleasing. Ticking things off is satisfying too, and it’s also synced to my iPad through iCloud so I always know what to do next. 

The fact it’s free is incredible, it’s a really high quality app that runs smoothly and looks so clean. I’m so grateful to the creators that the free version is absolutely viable on it’s own, it make me feel they truly want to make our lives easier! Thank you so much for this little app- whilst I certainly stray from the schedule more often than I’d like, have a frame for the day has helped me be so much more productive 🫶🏼

title: I wish I could give it more stars!!
body: I have ADHD and find a lot of tasks difficult to remember to do, or to remember if I’ve even done them (taking meds is a big one for me). This app is a game changer for that I can set things to reoccur (with the pro version) and I don’t miss things! No need to remember to write reoccurring stuff down (which is where other apps and physical planners let me down). I also love the widget because I am so bad about remembering to go into apps to check them. With the widget, I added it so it was always in my face which has worked so well.l for me. My husband is also so shocked with all the one off tasks I’m remembering to do. He normally needed to remind me several times about things and I would still forget. With this he makes sure I’ve added it to the app, because I can be bad with “writing things down” and the thing gets done. He says he feels less stressed knowing he doesn’t have to keep my to do list in his head. For me this app has everything I need and the look appeals to me which makes me want to use it. I think my only complaint regarding things the app doesn’t have are things the developer already has on their road map. But one thing not on their road map, which I’d find so helpful is a snooze option on tasks. I sometimes can be so busy and unable to get to a task that second. When that is the case it is easy to forget the task till I open the app. It would be wonderful if I could snooze the task for 15 minutes to be reminded it’s not done. But other than that this app is perfect and I’ve been singing its praises on how wonderful it is to anybody who will listen! I hope this review has been helpful and that you give the app a try!

title: Intuitive and feature packed
body: As someone who struggles with organisations I don’t have a lot of faith in planner apps, because they never seem to work for me or help me manage my productivity. And believe me, I've tested dozens. This app is the first of its kind in that regard; using it feels intuitive and logical, I’m able to keep track of my patterns with scheduled time, and I look forward to ticking daily tasks off. It has helped me maintain my study and art schedule and I’ve not had to reduce to sticking Post-It notes everywhere to keep me focussed! It has cute icons to categorise each task and splits events into Day vs Night which is a really handy feature most apps miss. Better yet, you can pick the distinction so for night owls and night workers, this still gives you flexibility. Overall, this app is awesome and run by a developer who really cares about the user experience.

author: Write a review today

title: In short GET THE APP!
body:
I am a uni student who suffers with ADHD & dyslexia.

If you can afford it please do pay the subscription because this creator deserves all the funding and help he can get to continue updating this app. And if your a working professional £8 isn’t really a lot for a year. 

And to the creator i want to say thank you for helping me out and allowing me to use your pro version on a support plan. I can see its already made a difference and once I'm back on a uni schedule it will save me loads of time and stress. 

Some thing i value the most about your app

the extensive customisation in terms of colour and icons for so many tasks ( colour coding always helps my memory)
The minute by minute time slots for precise time management planning
And if you’re interested i have a suggestion of an edit you can add which i personally know i would find really helpful. I know you have the inbox feature to jot down tasks that Don't yet have an allocated time slot in a specific day 

However my idea would be that you can also have a to do list section. Maybe it would appear at the bottom of each days on the calendar for thing that have to be done that day or reminders but don’t have a specific time stamp through out the day, such as pick up bread, or put your laundry on.  Just so its right there when you open your daily calendar as a reminder but don’t need it done at a specific time of the day.  

Other then that i have only praise for the app you created it has made my life easier so thank you for all the work you constantly put into this.

author: Ugo M

title: Clean and pretty but not for power users
body:
I don’t wish to be Mr Negative when this is essentially a smooth, clean and good-looking app but I do feel some balance/critique may be helpful in the light of several “greatest-of-all-time” style reviews in case people are hoping to ditch their more powerful todo manager or GTD style system for this offering. This app may be for you but I don’t think its intended for power users and that may be 100% by design.

If you are coming from a manual list or a simple list app then Structured is brimming with helpful features that you will value but if you are coming from (m)any of the established todo and GTD apps, you may find that ironically, given the name, what the app lacks is much in the way of structure for your tasks:

no tags (no way to group tasks that belong together, that happen at different times or are to be done by different people, different projects etc)
lists of sub-tasks are assumed to all take place on the same day which isn't much use for anything other than a shopping list or a recipe so I found this feature disappointing
only one folder (inbox) so no way to group items in a folder, No archive folder?
No share, print or email to tell others about a task or list of tasks
no search (I’m honestly unsure why would anyone create a database that you can’t search??)
In summary, if the idea of sharing or tagging your tasks or the idea that projects happen over multiple days/ with multiple people seems irrelevant (or terrifying) then you might just have found your ideal app. If you plan to manage anything beyond a daily routine or todays todos then you might need to look elsewhere.
Big shout out to the dev for a superUI and a clean/simple feel but personally I simply couldn’t give up a more powerful app for this yet - maybe version 2.0?

title: Wonderful App, but…
body:
App is beautiful, perfect, looks amazing, easy to use. I was ready to hit the purchase button but thought, wait till the watch is charged first, then test and see…

And I hit upon an issue that is sadly a deal breaker for me. To have the tasks show on my watch, iCloud has to be enabled/logged into. I simply can’t use iCloud, and I know I won’t be the only one in the same boat. Such a shame - perhaps in the future the reliance on iCloud to use the watch app will be done away with. 

To sync between phones, iPads and other ‘larger’ devices, iCloud is expected and is perfectly fair. To have to use iCloud to show tasks on a watch that is already directly connected to a phone with a constant connection seems backwards, and negates the whole point of the Apple Watch being an extension of the phone. 

For that one snag, I won’t be using Structured at this time for myself; having an easy to use app that is feature rich and shows my day/tasks on the watch as a complication was actually the one thing I was looking for above all else. Otherwise I only have good things to say about the app; the Developer seems to have put so much time, love and fairness into it, and it looks beautiful. If you already use iCloud and are looking for a daily schedule app, this is it. 

For me, it just isn’t there right now, but I will be keeping an eye on it for the future if the Watch app can be seamless and not rely on iCloud.

title: Great app and super useful but can be buggy

However, I’ve noticed that there are quite a few bugs when it comes to syncing with iCloud. The task colours and icons tend to change randomly, the timings I’ve set for a task change randomly and messes with the reminders app too. I’ve also noticed that when I’ve changed a date in the app, it sometimes won’t update through to reminders even though I’ve clicked the sync button. Sometimes it also automatically deletes a task, rather than cross it out.

It would be useful to have a default setting for syncing tasks e.g when you’ve edited a task within the app, it’s an inconvenience to keep clicking “sync with reminders”. I’d also like to see subtasks set on reminders to come through to the app as well. 

I’d happily pay extra for these to be implemented and I’d change my review from 3 to 5 stars when the bugs get fixed.

title: Recommend to everyone!
body:

Everything is customisable, all the features are simple to understand and use, and it has helpful little hints to keep you going. Watching a box slowly turn the colour you chose is incredibly satisfying, and it works excellently on a widget on my home screen, so I don’t need the app open to se my tasks. Notifications make sure I never forget, and I’ve never been to pleased to own an app that suits me and helps me stay on time (which has been a struggle thanks to ADHD)

I used to feel a little intimidated by a message in gaps saying “find something to do in this 30 minute break” but now they’ve changed to nice things like “take a break!” And “maybe find a book to read?” Which makes me feel comforted, and not shamed for when I do take a break.

When my contract with my school ends and this I-Pad becomes my own, I’ll be swapping it to my main I-Cloud, and purchasing the add-on (which is an INCREDIBLY cheap and affordable price, especially when you realise that the app runs NO adverts!) 

Full kudos to the creator, I’ve never felt so happy with a decision than getting this app.

title: Great app
body: I’ve recently started working full time and studying a degree part time. I’m also a very stubborn case of depression which means I need a little help to be on top of things. The app really helps see what downtime I have between tasks during the day, and really helps me seize the day as much as possible. The fact that I can tick the boxes as the day goes on means a lot as it gives me a visual guide of what I’ve done so far during the day, and helps prevent procrastination on days I feel down. I’m in a lot of debt from 2020/21 (long story, COVID related). I’d been going from app to app and using free trials and jumping onto the next. I really loved this one in particular because it’s so well designed in every way, and I saw there was an option to ask the developer to see if he could help me get the pro features as I can’t afford the price of the app at the moment. Within the same day he granted my request and I’m very grateful, there are no words to describe how much the app helps me, it’s like I’ve got my life back. I’ve recommended this to friends I think may benefit from it too so hopefully he will get some revenue this way. If ever he creates a way to donate rather than buy the app (as I have pro now anyway) I will be more than happy to donate the fair price for this app (which is definitely more than he’s even asking for pro) when I’m back on my feet.

title: Got My Life Sorted
body:
Been using Structured Pro for the last few few months and honestly, this app has overall made me more productive and more organised than I’ve ever been before. In a single day I’m able to make progress on multiple pieces of coursework and side projects as well as watch shows that I’ve been putting off.

Previously, I would write a general schedule on paper but found it to be inflexible and hard to keep track off. The Structured UI really helps me visualise how much time I have to complete a task and is very pleasing to look at especially with it’s customisable colours and icons.

I would give this app 5 stars if it were easier to rearrange tasks on the timeline in case there’s ever need to reschedule, so far I need to change the times on both tasks if I want to swap them around, although this is just nitpicking.
Another problem rests with interface for picking custom colours, there’s no obvious way to remove preset colours so you’re stuck with having to pick the right shade each time for a task (if you have a colour scheme in mind for certain types of tasks)

Overall, really good app ^^ I always recommend it to my friends.

The app is very well streamlined and looks nice, the colours and layout are not intimidating like so many planner apps and it makes you feel relaxed and ready for your next task, the small, non intrusive telling you how long you have until your next task are a great way of keeping you on track without stressing you out with endless reminders.
 
I really enjoy the range of customisation that you can do, including the icons for each task and which calendars are imported from your phone.

Simply put, the best calendar and organisation app I have ever used. And I have used many !

As someone with ADHD who has tried many different planning tactics, this seems like it will work the best for me, and for others !

title: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING APP AND SUCH A KIND CREATOR!
body: OMG right so where do I start!!!! This app is ABSOLUTELY amazing. Firstly, I love the way you have lain everything out in a way that is very simple but not too simple so it’s easy to direct yourself around however there are still LOADS of features to use. I set my own schedule everyday and this app helps so much with defeating lockdown boredome and feeling excited for the day ahead!! I have tried so many different apps like this but none of them have the right features I need- for example this shows the whole calendar of the month and then the whole schedule of the day in chronological order with the time at the side and even shows my wake up and bed time!!! It’s incredible how well all this is set out so you know exactly when your going to do something! I love the fact you can set your own SPECIFIC colour and tone for each task- this helps me work out what area of task I’m doing- for example pink I use as self care, green as work and jobs, etc. - this provides you with a very clear look of the day! And I LOVE the fact you can choose your own image for each task out of loads and loads of different ones to choose from! There’s always one which will fit with the activity and I think it’s so cool how the app can choose an icon for you- the one it think will fit!! These icons make the app so much more cute and fun and a lot more interesting!! It’s amazing how the app even tells you how long you might have a break between each task- this is sooooo helpful for me as sometimes I just need to know a set amount of time where I can relax and do nothing! I love how you can even set how long each task will be so you dont have to worry about calculating how long you’ll wait til your next task!! And best of all, PREMIUM IS EVEN BETTER!!! Due to personal reasons I couldn’t afford to download premium and I was so upset as I knew premium would impact my life (which hasn’t been going very well recently)- so like the app says, I message the extremely kind creator Leo and he offered a free premium for me!!!! I am so blessed to have someone do something taht kind for me and to everyone else out there who does have the money to afford premium- PLEASE GET IT!!- it is one of the BEST decisions you can make!! You can import all your different calendar events, the app will send you notifications for when to start your next task and SO MUCH MORE!! Leo deserves the money so much and as soon as I am privileged enough to have money to spend on this cause I will no doubtedly offer my savings to him. SO PLEASE PLEASE download this remarkable app!!!!!!!

title: A First Time User Opinion.
body:
I’ve been looking for a tasking/scheduling app for a while now but almost all of them are over-complicated and confusing. Before this I heavily relied on the calendar app for organising my day and writing lists for tasks. 

First things first, the design is super simple. It’s easy to navigate and user friendly. You can import events from your calendar, create new timed tasks and have them be recurring by day, month etc...and it allows you to check them off as you go. There are notifications when a new task or event begins and there’s even a widget! Really helpful to remind myself what I need to do next in my day.

The app has the functionality of a calendar, allowing you to schedule your working periods or appointments, but also allows you to add individual timed tasks into your schedule. I love this because you can see your day and remind yourself to do the washing when you get home, all in the same place. Best part is, it’s free!

Coffee’s on me ;)

Planning the week on Structured feels like a self care step rather than another executive functioning task. The visual timers are simple and exactly what I need and Apple Watch integration is seamless. The energy tracking feature is a great addition I haven’t seen in other apps. I appreciate that while the app does have AI integration it is easily disabled and doesn’t impact functionality. As someone who needs a strong visual planner as a daily disability aid, I find Structured to be intuitive, calming, and amazing value for money.

title: Disappointed With Structured
body:
I genuinely regret purchasing Structured’s lifetime plan, and based on my experience, I would not recommend this app to anyone looking for a reliable daily planner.

The biggest problem for me has been duplicate tasks and poor task-management workflow. Instead of saving me time, the app has made my daily planning more frustrating. I have had to fix tasks and adjust things manually again and again, defeating the entire purpose of using a productivity app.

I bought the lifetime plan expecting a dependable planner that would help me organise my entire day. Instead, I feel that I wasted my money on an app that creates additional work rather than reducing it.

What made the experience even worse was the refusal to refund my purchase, despite my dissatisfaction with the app. I understand that refund policies exist, but being left with a product that does not work well for my needs and no refund has been extremely disappointing.

A productivity app should make life simpler, not force users to spend more time correcting their schedule. Before buying the lifetime plan, please test the app thoroughly with your own workflow, especially if you rely on Apple Reminders and use multiple Apple devices.

My advice: Take the free version and trial seriously before spending money. Do not assume that the lifetime plan is worth it just because it is a one-time purchase. I learned this the hard way, and I hope other users do their research before making the same decision.

title: Structured – A Clean and Practical Way to Organize Your Day
body:
Structured is a thoughtfully designed productivity app that focuses on simplicity and clarity. Unlike many overly complex planning tools, it provides a straightforward way to organize daily tasks using a visual timeline, making it easy to understand how your day is structured at a glance.

One of its strongest features is the time-based layout, which allows users to plan their day in a realistic and manageable way. This approach helps improve focus and reduces the chances of overloading your schedule. The interface is clean, intuitive, and free from unnecessary distractions, which enhances the overall user experience.

The app is also flexible enough to adapt to different routines. Whether you are managing studies, work, or personal tasks, it allows you to customize your schedule, set reminders, and stay consistent with your plans. Additionally, the smooth performance and reliable syncing across devices ensure that your schedule remains accessible wherever you are.

Overall, Structured is a well-balanced productivity tool that combines simplicity with effectiveness. It is especially suitable for users who prefer a minimal yet powerful way to manage their time and daily activities.
author: Chiragemforriot

title: Review
body:
I’ve been using Structured for a while now, and it’s easily one of the best productivity apps on the App Store. The clean interface, intuitive design, and seamless time-blocking features make planning my day effortless. It helps me stay focused, organized, and actually follow through on my tasks without feeling overwhelmed.

What I really love is how visually clear everything is — you can see your entire day mapped out, which makes managing time so much easier. The reminders and flexibility to adjust tasks on the go are also a huge plus.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to boost productivity and bring structure to their daily routine. Definitely a 5-star app!

title: Nice idea POOR support
body: It’s missing so many intuitive key features that any natural calendar or task management app must have. (i) if event descriptors are too long the hide buttons are buried outside of screen so you can’t hide event (ii) no way to remove completed tasks from your day view so that next task is on focus (iii) unnecessary huge UI elements - use on 27 inch iMac and you know it’s full of wasted space (iv) cumbersome way to view months ahead as you can’t really scroll entire month view (v) unintuitive design for viewing all tasks upcoming in a week (vi) if you look at some day in past no obvious way to jump directly to “today” view. I can’t believe I paid for lifetime sub of this app. Horribly made and nothing like feature list suggests. It will add to anxiety not reduce!

title: Impressive Start!
body:
I've just started using the Structured app today, and I must say, I'm quite impressed. As a first-day user, here are my initial thoughts:

User-Friendly Interface: The app's interface is clean, intuitive, and easy to navigate. I didn't encounter any difficulties in finding my way around, which is a big plus.

Sleek Design: The design is sleek and visually appealing. It's clear that the developers have put thought into creating a polished app.

Effective Organization: Structured lives up to its name by providing a well-organized platform for managing tasks, schedules, and notes. The customizable categories make it easy to tailor the app to my specific needs.

Syncing and Backup: I appreciate the seamless syncing across devices and the option for backups. Knowing that my data is safe and accessible on various devices is reassuring.

Performance: So far, the app has been snappy and responsive. No noticeable lag or crashes during my initial use.

Learning Curve: Although the app is user-friendly, it might take a little time to explore all the features and get the most out of it. A brief tutorial or onboarding process could be helpful for newcomers.

Overall, my first day with Structured has been quite promising. I'm looking forward to exploring more of its features and seeing how it enhances my productivity. Great job, developers!

title: Structured: The Minimalist App That Maximizes Productivity!
body:
Structured is a top-tier productivity app that boasts a sleek and minimalist design, coupled with an impressive set of features that enable users to easily structure their day. The app is designed to be as straightforward and user-friendly as possible, eliminating the need for any unnecessary tabs or complicated features. Despite this simplicity, Structured manages to provide a wide range of functions, making it a robust choice for anyone looking for a productivity app.

One of the most impressive aspects of Structured is its seamless integration and sync features. The app integrates easily with other apps, ensuring that you can always stay up-to-date with your tasks and schedule. Additionally, the app provides a range of features that allow for the customization of tasks, making it easy to manage complex projects or to-do lists.

Another standout feature of Structured is its accessibility. The app's simplistic and clean view is easy to navigate, making it accessible to users with disabilities and those who are neurodivergent. The app is also compatible with screen readers, and Apple's dynamic text, making it ideal for users who require larger text on the app.

Overall, Structured is an outstanding app that provides a perfect balance between simplicity and robustness. The app is user-friendly, accessible, and customizable, making it an ideal choice for anyone looking to streamline their day-to-day activities. I highly recommend downloading this app.

title: Amazing but has massive scope for improvement
body:
Hey Leo,
Been using this app for about 2 weeks now and I love it!

Here are a few ideas that come to mind to make the experience even better:

- Apple Watch integration: For people using the Apple Watch, having a complication on the Watch face would be very convenient to see upcoming tasks. At least Siri Watch Face integration would be very nice to have.

- Creating calendar events (not just import): Right now, I need to have another app to create events and meetings on my calendar and then get it imported to Structured. I feel having the ability to directly create the even in app would be a huge time saver and possible attract a larger audience.

Togliere all’improvviso una funzionalità base ed essenziale, usata gratuitamente per anni e bloccarla dietro a un paywall è stata una brutta sorpresa. 
La sincronizzazione con i propri strumenti principali non dovrebbe essere considerata una funzionalità premium. 
Sono molto delusa e dato che ora è diventata inutilizzabile per me la disinstallerò. Un vero peccato visto che la grafica e l’interfaccia mi piacevano molto.

title: Tra le migliori app per il time-boxing
body:
Buona esperienza utente grazie alla progettazione di un flusso incentrato sui giusti user requirements (creazione e personalizzazione dei singoli tasks, pianificazione dell’intera giornata, personalizzazione). La cosa migliore, infatti, è che le features principali sono quasi tutti incluse nella versione free.

Ottima la possibilità di selezionare il tipo di “ambiente” tra default, simplified e minimal, così da evitare il carico cognitivo.

Da rivedere alcune scelte di design per quanto riguarda la UI, ma in generale l’interfaccia è ben fatta.

title: Buona app ma può ancora migliorare
body:
Uso Structured ormai da diverso tempo, mi è piaciuta da subito e ho fatto anche l'upgrade a pro. 
Stupenda dal punto di vista dell'interfaccia, ha una estetica davvero bella e ordinata. Mi piace molto la personalizzazione che si può effettuare. Do 3 stelle perchè penso che ci siano delle cose da migliorare.
Innanzitutto l'app si blocca spesso sul Mac e sono stata costretta più volte ad eseguire l'uscita forzata. Per me oltre alla risoluzione di questa problematica sarebbe molto importante lo sviluppo di una visione mensile e settimanale che sia coerente con l'estetica. Una cosa pittosto fastidiosa è che quando vado a scrivere il nome dell'attività avendo prima selezionato l'icona quest'ultima non rimane salvata e cambia. L'operazione di selezione dell'icona non è facile da eseguire in quanto ogni volta che scorro il pannello in questione avviene un forte rallentamento. Anche la sincronizzazione tra mac e iphone nel mio caso devo dire che è davvero lenta. Insomma, questa app ha già aspetti positivi ma potrebbe essere notevolmente migliorata!

Quello che manca è però la possibilità di definire due o più programmi settimanali, ad esempio quello che faccio di solito in città magari è diverso da quello che faccio quando torno dai miei ecc. Quindi sarebbe bello switchare tra i due, senza essere costretti a modificare l'intero timetable. Secondo me questa è la grande mancanza in questa applicazione.

It would be wonderful and essential to have data shared via email accounts, as is the case with Google Drive and the like, perhaps even only for the pro versions. Too bad, it would be irreplaceable!

title: Da 0 a 100

Mi ha permesso di sfruttare al meglio ogni giornata e posso ri-schedulare senza problemi le attività che non riesco a portare a termine in una giornata. 
Completamente personalizzabile, ha tutte le funzioni che una persona può sognare.
 Mi ha permesso letteralmente di portare le mie giornate da 0 a 100. Consigliatissima!!

Molto focalizzata alla concentrazione, è ottima anche per tenere traccia dei tempi spesi su un determinato progetto. Sul mio iPhone 14 pro posso vedere la durata del task sulla lock screen in modalità always on. Ampiamente configurabile e curata nei minnimi dettagli come il colore del tema e delle icone. Per il resto è un planner piuttosto valido.

title: La migliore! + suggerimento
body:
Quest’applicazione è probabilmente la migliore che ho trovato. Permette con una semplicità incredibile di programmare le proprie giornate e il sistema di notifica personalizzabile è molto utile e per niente invadente.

L’unico aspetto che potrebbe essere migliorato è l’organizzazione delle task, consentendo cioè di creare delle nested task composte da più attività più piccole con il proprio tempo. Faccio un esempio:
- Allenamento (1h)
   - Riscaldamento (10 minuti)
   - Corsa (40 minuti)
   - Stretching (10 minuti)
Questo si potrebbe implementare o dando la possibilità di creare una gerarchia per le task –come negli elenchi puntati complessi – oppure mettendo la possibilità di aggiungere una durata e delle notifiche alle sotto-attività che pure possono essere inserite. 

A parte questo piccolo suggerimento, apprezzo versamento tanto la versatilità e la semplicità di questa applicazione, che consente sviluppare in contemporanea un compito e dargli una collocazione temporale – la base del time blocking – e quindi può essere usata da tutti – studenti, professionisti, atleti, lavoratori etc. Ho pagato volentieri i 10 euro dell’iscrizione al Pro per la versione Mac e sono rimasto di sasso quando ho scoperto che in quanto ‘early adopter’ la versione di iOS mi era stata regalata. Ma dovessi pagherei anche quei dieci euro. Grazie davvero Leo!

title: Casi perfecta!
body:
La he estado usando desde 2024 para planear toda mi rutina desde que me despierto hasta dormir. Es una gran herramienta para medir tiempos y organizarte de la mejor manera. Los widgets son muy buenos. En mi opinión le faltan 2 cosas:
- Un habit tracker
- Si yo pudiera hacer una lista de tareas y de esa lista simplemente configurar las que se irán repitiendo en mi semana en diferentes horarios. Por ejemplo, si voy al gym los martes a las 2 y los jueves a las 5… etc. Para no tener que estar repitiendo el proceso de agregar tareas.
Además cuando quiero agregar una tarea me aparecen sugerencias de tareas que hice una vez hace mucho, estaría bien si se pudieran quitar las sugerencias. Pero fuera de eso me encanta!

title: PLEASE ADD THIS AND IT'LL BE 5 STARS
body:
Hi! Premium lifetime user here since like 2 weeks ago. I like the app but is missing something really important for me: for example when you get a notification in Apple Reminders and you open the app Apple Reminders, the notification persists, so you won't miss that for any reason, even if you skipped that task for that day.

In Structured, notifications doesn’t work the same, because they get “deleted” when you open the app. Please add an option to make the notifications don't get deleted when the user opens the app. Please!

title: Que pésima experiencia la sincronización.
body:
Desde un inicio me dio mucho problema sincronizar, pero ya había quedado todo cool…

Hoy quise ver eventos desde mi Apple Watch y no funcionó, quedo en SYNC y nunca sincronizó nada. 

Sus tontas soluciones de problemas dice que desinstales en todos tus dispositivos, cierres sesión y vuelvas a entrar. 

Lo hice muy a mi pesar, desinstalando en mi MacBook, iPad y iPhone, y ¡oh sorpresa!!! Ahora no sincroniza nada y me marca error y error ahora en TODOS MIS DISPOSITIVOS!!!!!

Que bueno que solo lo quise probar al mes, porque quería pagar el año. 

Pésima app en sincronización con mis demás dispositivos.

title: Me encanta la aplicacion pero..
body:
En general es una aplicación genial que me ha ayudado mucho a organizarme y a lograr llevar a cabo mis tareas durante el día sin saturarme. La adoro mucho y aparte tiene una interfaz super linda. Mil gracias por hacer aplicaciones tan buenas que ayudan a la gente  a dejar de procrastinar.

Me encantaria que implementaran una función de que en la laptop se pudieran arrastrar las tareas de un dia a otro mas facilmente, (que se vea toda la semana y no solo un dia para así hacerlo mas facilmente); asi como cambiar la duración de la tarea  arrastrandola con el mouse para  ya que la interfaz de la laptop da para hacer estas cosas a diferencia del telefono; y por ultimo estaria genial que hubiera un botón automático para posponer tareas para el dia siguiente ya que si no te da tiempo de algo y quieres pasarlo para otro día es un poco tedioso pasarlo para el dia siguiente, aunque no es imposible, pero así sería más fácil. 

Espero que les sirva la retroalimentación, en general es una maravillosa aplicación. Recomendadisima.

title: A Game Changer for Daily Organization!

I love how Structured allows me to create different categories for tasks, whether it’s work-related, personal errands, or even leisure activities.

title: It’s good but everything takes too long
body:
I’ve used To-Doist, Akiflow, Asana, Google Calendar and others and I do really like this one but some things just take too much time to quickly edit compared to others. If I want to edit a task and add some subtasks, I need to go into Edit, scroll all the way down and then edit and it doesn’t detect lists so you have to go one by one. Most importantly is being able to edit sub tasks on the go. 

Also I can’t figure out how to add things to inbox quickly from the Mac App. Only if the inbox is empty you can add an item but after that I can’t figure out to add something to Inbox instead of the selected day.

Lastly, changing time on a task means you have to go to Edit, and then change the duration. Changing the time is also a different window and currently doesn’t work. Also a let down.

Other than that it’s a good app, I just wish it was a bit sleeker.

title: Niet echt klantvriendelijk
body:
Ik wilde deze app uitproberen voor een speciale functie waar ik het abonnement voor nodig had. 
Prima, maar na het afsluiten bleek deze functie anders te werken dan wat ik verwacht had. 
Refund aangevraagd bij Apple, werd afgewezen. En dat binnen twee dagen na aanschaf van deze app. 
Contact opgenomen met de klantenservice van Structured, alles uitgelegd, ook dat ik de juiste stappen heb gezet richting Apple en ik op de hoogte ben dat alle klantgegevens en betalingen via Apple gaan. Maar ook dat er bedrijven zijn die uit klantvriendelijkheid toch een refund verstrekken ondanks dat Apple dat niet doet. Kreeg hierop een vrij standaard antwoord waarop totaal niet werd ingegaan op mijn inhoud van mijn bericht. Wel zat er een link bij naar Apple support. Maar daar had ik het dus al tweemaal geprobeerd. 
Vervolgens geen reactie meer vanuit Structured. 
Twee sterren omdat de app er wel netjes uitziet, maar uiteindelijk niet voor mijn wensen geschikt is. En de klantenservice niet heel behulpzaam is.

title: So far one of the best planning apps I’ve come across, especially when you have ADHD.
body:
I got my ADHD diagnosis almost a year ago, but I’ve been struggling all my life to find a planning system that works for me. 

I like that there’s a visual of how much time there’s left for a task, that you can check it off and that you can put notes or subtasks. There’s a lot of room for customization if you want to as well. 

I’ve been contemplating to upgrade because some very useful features are sadly locked but understandably so. Luckily you can ask for a scholarship discount. I finally applied after months of procrastinating. I hope it’s possible. I really want to support this business because its a great app, but I’m currently a student and not able to work much after school. I do hope I can support in the future!

I have one recommendation which is to be able to make lists/maps in the inbox thing because you can give colours but then you have to scroll through it and I just feel like being able to make a map for for example school tasks or chores or fun things to do would be very nice.

title: Great planning app
body:
I really like this planning app. Helps me to remind and to plan activities that should be done very efficiently in contrast to a to do list. Some improvement could be made on replanning. I’d like to see that I could more easily switch the tasks. For example if one task took more time, I’d like all other tasks of the same color (or type) to add that time as well. Same for rearranging. 
I’d also think that it would help me if tasks overlap, it would take new branch of the so I could see the time that it overlaps. For example sometimes I’m doing a task of two hours and in between I have to make a call. I don’t want that task of two hours to be split in two tasks, I’d like to see the task of making a call on a adjacent track.
Overall the app helps me a lot in planning a lot better and have control over the day. I use the pro for the reminders app as a backlog and it works great. With the improvements suggested I’d think I’d rate it at least 7 stars

title: Eindelijk!
body:
Een app met vrijwel alles in een. Een erg soepele synchronisatie met andere apps. Het gebruiksgemak is een dikke tien. Voor iemand met bijvoorbeeld adhd is de app fijn. Veelal zie je dat je aparte apps van elkaar moet gebruiken. Denk aan Outlook: mail en agenda in een app, maar de ‘taken’ in een andere app. Echt super vervelend vind ik dat en dit zorgt voor het vergeten van dingen. Structured heeft het, zoals ik het kan zien, andersom: taken en kunnen synchroniseren met je agenda. Meestal heb je namelijk meer taken dan afspraken… 

Er is natuurlijk altijd ruimte voor verbetering. wellicht zitten deze opties al wel in de app, maar heb ik het nog niet gevonden: Een Agenda-afspraak maken in Structured. Ik zet nu een ‘taak’ weg als ‘afspraak’ en dit werkt op zich prima. Voor mij zou het fijn zijn wanneer je het echt als afspraak kunt invoeren. Iets is een taak wanneer het niet langer dan 30 minuten duurt. Hierna wordt het een ‘afspraak’. De meest gebruikte symbolen bovenaan zetten wanneer je een symbool kunt kiezen. 

Voor het symbool ‘bellen’ moet je behoorlijk zoeken. Een uitroepteken als symbool zou ik ook heel prettig vinden. 

De app beschikbaar maken voor MacBook, zodat ik op elk apparaat toegang heb tot de agenda. Iets wat ik persoonlijk heel praktisch vind: het delen van de agenda en dat de ander ook afspraken of taken erin kan zetten. Voor een gezin zou dit heel fijn zijn. De app heeft een nette prijs voor onbeperkt toegang en de prijs is eenmalig. Deze combinatie zie ik zeer weinig. 

 Toevoeging: de widget ververst niet meer, terwijl deze functie wel aanstaat in mijn instellingen. Nu is voor mij een belangrijke functie weg. Heb gemaild, maar ik krijg geen reactie 😖

title: Great, but some issues
body:
I love the app. Planning my time is a more healthy way of going about my day than setting goals and threatening to-do lists. Planning time blocks and getting reminders is great, and I love the inbox function especially on the Mac app to see what I have yet to schedule.

Unfortunately I have some syncing issues with the app though. After not opening the app for a few hours, it forgets that I have the Pro version and it prompts me to go though the initial set-up again. It then plants the ‘instruction tasks’ in between my already existing tasks. Also, when I make changes in the tasks on my phone and then open my Mac app (or vice versa), the app shows both the old and new tasks overlapping. This can only be solved by manually rearranging and deleting the tasks. My guess is that this problem would be fixed with some smoother cloud syncing. 

No hard feelings though. I appreciate the app and the fact that you are a small developer. I am thankful for the one-time payment, since not everyone can afford expensive subscriptions. I would love to keep using the app, but I would like to see some improvement of the syncing issues.

title: Mangler noen essensielle funksjoner
body:
Jeg liker appen. Jeg elsker den faktisk. Men den har noen funksjoner jeg savner så inderlig mye, som gjør at jeg faktisk ikke kan bruke den (enda). Jeg har sjekket FeatureBase, og jeg ser mange forslag på tingene jeg savner. Frem til disse funksjonene kommer, vil jeg dessverre ikke bruke denne.
Det jeg savner mest er:
1. Deling mellom partner/familie - denne funksjonen gjør at jeg ikke kan bruke appen. Jeg må ha en app som har alt, og denne har ikke det.
2. Habit-tracker - Gjerne med 7-dagers/30-dagers visual report som noen skrev på forbedringssiden deres.
Ellers enn det elsker jeg muligheten for å kjøpe appen med life-time kjøp, og jeg kommer til å kjøpe så fort deling mellom brukere er satt opp. Jeg elsker også at kalenderen er så oversiktlig. Appen er nesten perfekt!

body:
I bought the premium version in order to be able to import calendars. Turns out there is no calendar widget, which was the reason in wanted this app. In the app information it says that it is available in a multitude of languages, but it is set to the language of your phone, which means for me badly word-for-word translated Norwegian (I’d rather have it in English than crappy Norwegian). When you change the language, the titles stay in your phone’s language, so every time I open the app I have to see that ridiculous “stå opp og skinne” which is obviously a direct translation of “stand up and shine”.
Most of the other functions this app offers work just as find on OneNote, so I just threw away money on a yearly subscription.

title: Dette er hvorfor jeg liker appen.
body:
Hei, Jeg ville komme med en tilbakemelding fordi appen er veldig fin og ideen er bra. 
Jeg liker at den fortsatt er brukbar selvom den inneholder kjøp i app. Du må absolutt ikke ha premium for at den skal funke optimalt. 
Selv er jeg en person som sliter litt med og holde orden og Structured har hjelpet meg med akkurat dette.
Jeg liker konseptet og måten dere utførte appen på er veldig bra, spør du meg. 
Håper at i fremtiden så kommer dere ut med flere apper, ville veldig gjerne hatt enda flere funksjoner i dette også. Eks: bare for trenings-plan, døgnrytme eller jobben din. Siden nå er kanskje alt litt blandet (eller det er bare en linje for alt sammen) selvom jeg er informert om at du kan bruke denne linjen for hva som helst.)
Så egentlig har jeg ingen klager, denne appen er verdt å laste ned og har hjelpet å få ut den positive i meg!) veldig glad i appen fordi den har virkelig mange gode verdier☺️

title: Fantastic scheduling app!
body:
This app has been so useful for me! I have raging ADHD but I work better with a schedule, so I would always write one on a piece of paper, and forget about it after a couple of days. Plus, if anything changed from the schedule it would all get thrown out for the day, because it was too difficult to fit new things around it. This app solves all the problems I have with this! 

I can set up my whole week’s schedule, to be recurring week in week out, and the app will always pop up to remind me to move to the next task, go eat dinner, start winding down to bed, etc. I spent so long looking for an app like this, and I’m so glad I’ve found one! Thank you to the developers for making it accessible for people on shoestring budgets too, it’s really appreciated.

title: LOVE IT!  ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
body:
I’ve never left a review for any other app but this one…. I had to because it’s that AMAZING! Some of the things I love about the app is:

-  ‘Inbox’ I love that I can brain dump everything here and schedule a time and date when it has one but it keeps it of my head so I’m not stressing about it. 
- ‘Subtask’ I love that I can have a main heading and have all these little tasks listed under it which makes it look/ feel less overwhelming because you can’t actually see them on the calendar view. 
- It’s super cute!!! The colours, icons…. EVERYTHING! 
- Being able to see gaps in between tasks so you can maximise your time. Also the little motivational sayings to fill your time. 

I’ve downloaded so many productivity/ organisation apps but I would always fall out of using them because they never had all the features needed to keep using it BUT this one does!!!! Super impressed

I’ve tried many planner apps, but Structured App Daily Planner is by far the most convenient and user-friendly one I’ve come across! The intuitive design makes scheduling tasks effortless, and the seamless integration with my calendar helps me stay organized like never before.

What truly sets this app apart is its clean interface, smart notifications, and easy-to-use features, making time management a breeze. Whether you’re planning your day, setting reminders, or organizing long-term goals, Structured makes everything so simple and efficient!

A huge THANK YOU to the team for offering a one-year free scholarship to access Pro/Premium features! It’s incredibly generous and allows more people to experience the full potential of the app without financial barriers.

I highly recommend Structured App Daily Planner to anyone looking for an effective and stress-free way to stay on top of their schedule! 💙

title: Structured - Daily Planner
body:

title: Få saker gjorda!
body:
Det här är ett kraftfullt och mysigt verktyg för personlighetstyper som har svårt med igångsättning och planering av sin tid. Eller personer som bara vill ha ett bra planeringsverktyg för små-saker som ”aldrig blir gjorda”. Appen gör det roligt att få saker och ting gjorda, och gör det enkelt att planera in saker man måste göra.

Kommer man på något som måste göras? Bara att lägga det i Inkorgen och planera in det sen. Att man också kan mäta energiåtgång om man vill på ett så enkelt sätt, för att se om det blir för mycket inplanerat under en dag, är också så otroligt användbart. Allt uppdateras utan problem via iCloud så man kan titta i iPad och Mac också om man har möjlighet och vill det. Fokus-funktionen, där man ser hur lång tid det är kvar av en aktivitet, är också en guld-funktion i vissa aktiviteter som känns tråkiga, så att man står ut med att göra klart. Och när man är klar med en uppgift så bockar man av den, den stryks över samtidigt som ett trevligt ljud ploppar till, otroligt tillfredsställande.

Ska man nämna några nackdelar så skulle det vara att appen verkar dra lite mer batteri än andra appar, och att den fortfarande verkar ha en del buggar där jag t.ex. lagt till saker i Inkorgen som inte hamnat där förrän jag startat om appen. Men tillverkarna arbetar hela tiden på uppdateringar, så det kommer dom säkert fixa med tiden.

Det tog några dagar, sedan insåg jag att jag kommer leva med den här appen.

Jag måste rekommendera den här appen å det varmaste om man har en personlighetstyp där man inte får saker och ting gjorda, t.ex. om man har svårt med igångsättning, adhd, add, autism osv. Jag rekommenderar den även som en mer allmän planeringskalender till alla, då med fokus på grejer som ska göras men aldrig blir gjorda. 

Stort tack till tillverkarna av den här appen som har förenklat mitt och många andras liv!

title: Great app!
body:
Structure makes it very easy to create and follow routines! It allows you to plan your day hour by hour, and to keep track on which activities are completed by checking them. You can also make sub-activities to every activity and then check them as well when they are completed, super useful! It’s easy to repeat the different activities on specific days, or make them only appear once. Another function I like is the separate check list with activities that needs to be done, but without deadline. Recently I noticed that you can also decide how energy-demanding different activities on your schedule are, and experiment with how much work/rest you need each day. Great idea!

However, there is also one function I'm missing. While Structured is great for creating routines, it is not very good for getting an overview of more flexible activities coming up within the next month.  So for example, if I create an activity and put it into the schedule that I will study from 8 to 12 each day, I can't switch to an overview of the entire month where I can easily see what “studying” means each day. Like; am I having an exam, a deadline, a meeting, or class? Such a function is crucial when you are planning several weeks ahead and need to see your plans month by month. With such a function Structured would get 5/5 stars from me!

body:

It did not take into account the few things I had added to the schedule myself, making it useless since it’s suggestions just asumed I didn’t have any commitments and didn’t plan around them. I tried using it for productivity since I wanted to copy my schedule to the following week so I don’t have to manually tell the tasks to repeat but it didn’t understand those instructions.

Other than that the app is very intuitive and choosing icons and colors helps me a lot when I look at the schedule. It imports my appointments from my iOS calender which is great, and it does this automatically the second I add something (accept an event invite via text etc.). 

It suggests the tasks I have already inputed for other days and editing the time I do them is easy. 

Great app, AI needs a lot of work but I look forward to when it is actually usable.

title: Some changes are needed for sure
body:
Hi Structured team,

First, thank you for creating such an amazing app. Structured has become my main app for planning my day because I love the timeline view and how easy it is to organize my schedule.

One feature that I think would make the app even better is custom colors for events and tasks.

Right now, if I create all of my events directly in Structured (school, church, CCA, appointments, etc.), they all look very similar. Apple Calendar events can have different colors based on their calendar, but native Structured events cannot.

It would be incredibly helpful if users could:

* Assign a color to individual events or tasks.
* Or create categories/calendars (e.g. School, Exercise, Church, Personal) with their own colors.
* Optionally filter or view events by these categories.

For example, I’d love to quickly distinguish:

* 🔵 School
* 🟢 Sports / CCA
* 🟣 Church
* 🟠 Personal
* 🔴 Important events

This would make the timeline much easier to scan at a glance, especially for students and people who use Structured as their primary planning app.

Thank you for all the work you put into Structured. I hope you’ll consider adding this feature in a future update!
