title: Solid app but a few small things that make it difficult to use
body:
I want to start by saying that this app is really great and has a lot of features that I like but this review is mostly the things that will likely keep me from using this. I got the pro plan for a month to test this out before committing. I do like a lot of the organization features but here are the things I wish the developers would improve upon: 
1. There is no way to shift your whole day- if you get up an hour later or have to add something in your schedule you have to manually move every task which is time consuming.
2. Piggy backing on #1, it would be nice to be able to mark a task as time sensitive or not. For instance- this is an appointment that cannot be moved vs. I would like to eat lunch at 1:00 but it could be moved if I needed to move it. 
3. There doesn’t seem to be a way to set tasks for certain days of the week like M-F. There is a workaround where I could add the same task for every day and make it weekly- but again, that’s time consuming and defeats the purpose of the app making your life easier. 
4. The app it’s quite responsive enough and the timing aspect of it can be more stressful than helpful. If you haven’t checked a task off in time the app just moves on to the next thing. It makes me feel bad for falling behind. I wish it was a bit more responsive and would adjust when you fall behind or ask if you want to move the task or delay it by a day. There’s no way to roll tasks over which is just very unrealistic. 
Overall this app is at about 80% of what I would want out of a planning app. Seems to work well for a lot of people but I’m still on the hunt for one that is more helpful and less work for me to keep organized. As much as I love the idea of a planning app I still find that a paper bullet journal is the easiest and least time consuming way to plan my day.

title: PERFECT FOR STUDENTS & ADHD
body:
I am a college student with late diagnosed ADHD and I have ALWAYS been unable to manage my time & assignments. I got this app with the pro version and it may be the most important app to me on my phone!!! I put in ALL my assignments, when I see my friends, and personal routines/appointments on here and it helps me keep track of what I’m doing. This app reminds me that I’m way more productive than I think I am.

I love that it has a very simple interface and it’s so easy to use. Basically everything is customizable in terms of icons and colors, which makes it so fun/easy to label and color code different types of activities. Lately my favorite feature has been the inbox tool because I pop any idea I have like “call (person) about (whatever)” or anything that seems small, but it’s important for me to remember.

title: So many positives, bought the Pro version!
body: I RARELY write reviews for things. If I write a review it's either because the product has made a monumental impact on my life or it completely failed to lived up to its expectations. This app has definitely made a monumental impact on my life. I am neurodivergent (autistic/ADHD) and really have trouble remembering what needs done throughout the day. Even if I write a list or set alarms on my phone....I still don't get things done. This app has changed that in a big way for me. My calendar appointments show up on it so I can easily see those on the daily schedule while I'm planning out my day and adding tasks in where I need to get them completed. The addition of the check bubble to check off when you have completed the task or appointment is extremely helpful for me. I am a visual person and need to see what I've completed, what I still need to do, and at what time. I can drag tasks around the day to change the time in case I run behind on something. It is such a simple feature that I didn't realize I needed until I used it. You can set alerts for things such as when to start a task, when it's done, when it's almost time to stop, etc. This is like the best calendar and to-do list wrapped into one. It ahs a focus mode so when you need to work on a task you can put it in focus mode so you don't mess with your phone. LOVE THAT. I used this app for 2 days before I realized it was definitely worth trying out the Pro version and I went ahead and purchased the lifetime Pro version and do not regret it. Absolutely worth it. If I could hi-five or hug this developer, I would. I'm staying on task, managing my time much better, and getting things done. This has been life changing for me. Which is crazy when I think about it...a planner app has changed my life...but it definitely has. THANK YOU FOR MAKING THIS AND THANK YOU FOR ALL OF THE CONTINUED WORK YOU DO TO STRIVE TO CONTINOUSLY IMPROVE THE APP!

title: This app is what all indie apps should be!
body: I adore this app - lovely design, great functionality, great quality for the price. The support team helped me get going when I had trouble with a promotional offer, and it's so hard to find an app that is responsive with such good service. This is a generous offering for what you get for the paid platform, and is still completely functional with the free options. I love the integrations with my apps (Notes, Calendar), I love the new feature for click-and-drag tasks. It's a great app for anyone with ADHD or who just needs a little extra help with visually organizing their day. I use mine mostly to reference when I did things and what got done, and it isn't really intended for that, so sometimes the functionality doesn't work great for it, but I would absolutely recommend this to a friend (and have many times!). My only real issue with the app is that the color options are different across devices - the colors on the app don't match the colors on desktop for me, and I usually wind up having to make notes of the hex code for which color I used. I wish there was a way to favorite colors and icons and/or note their specific uses, because it is a little bit of a pain to go back and try to find those again if they aren't picked up by the SmartIcon feature. Still, none of that deserves to mark down such a great app, and hopefully it's something that the developers will be able to adjust for over time. I'll absolutely be renewing for another year, and I can't wait to see where they go with it over time!

title: Love!!
body:
I am crazy about this app.  So many things I love about it . . . 

Love the colors; makes you want to use it.

It has a fantastic layout where it’s very clear what you plan to do that day; those are the scheduled tasks.  BUT, the great thing is, on the side panel, you can write in all the other things you want to do, but haven’t scheduled yet.  Brilliant!

It has all sorts of reminders.  I love the sound reminders!  I am a writer and once I get involved in something I remember absolutely nothing, so the alarm going off is critical for me.

It’s super easy to reschedule things.  For example, I exercise every second day, and once I enter Exercise, I can set it to repeat, if I want to.

I have yet to explore the many other options.  For me, more than anything, it’s an interface that works for me and that I LOVE to use.  And it works to do exactly what I want it to do, highlight important stuff that I absolutely want to do and remind me to do it.

Oh, one more thing — I don’t know much about coding, but this seems so well built, quick, pretty, efficient.  Looks fantastic.  And the company seems absolutely wonderful; wonderful people.

Very happy I found this app.  Thank you!!

author: Atomic Super Girl

title: One easy step away from being perfect
body: I am an adult with severe ADHD and struggle with staying on task throughout the day due to time blindness, distractions and horrible short term memory. I’ve downloaded and tried nearly every well reviewed calendar and planning app I can find and can easily say none of them compare to the clean, simple, customizable UI of this one. The constant start/end reminders, color coding, customization and live visual of how much time is left with each task are simple things that are life changing for someone with ADHD, and likely plenty of non-ADHDers. Seeing these options, I quickly subscribed to the annual year plan and started setting up daily systems to keep me on track. The one major flaw that is forcing me to continue with google calendar/tasks rather than this app is that there is no option to repeat tasks on specific days. For example, setting a task to repeat only on Tuesdays & Thursdays, M-F or only on one specific day of the week or repeat on a specific day of the month. My schedule varies throughout the week and I have drastically different schedule and routine on weekends. Being forced to manually input everything for every single weekday & every single weekend or having my weekday tasks repeat “everyday” is quite the shortfall. Daily manual input takes away the efficiency & automation of systematic routines & having weekday task reminders repeated on weekends, is quite the nuisance. If the option becomes available to select specific days of the week for reoccurring tasks, I will quickly edit this review to be 5-stars, recommend to everyone and switch to relying on this app for staying on track. I hope to see this update very soon because this app is otherwise incredible and I really want to put it to use. Having only one complaint, though it’s a bit of a make or break for me, the developers have done an amazing job with this planner. Keep it up.

author: Lexzues

title: Halfway there!
body:
So much of it is good, but I’ll start with the bad in order of importance:

1. Slow performance! Takes literally 2 seconds to just add an icon to a task. There are examples of this all across the app.

2. No way to apply custom gature. Having properties for subtasks would indeedrouping or organization of any kind. This is especially an issue when importing Apple Reminders. This is actually a deal breaker for me. I have so many unscheduled tasks that I like to keep in folders to stay organized. So pretty much I can’t use Structured right now.

3. No Google Calendar integration. As far as calendar integrations go, this one is essential since work-related events aren’t likely to be in your Apple Calendar.

4. No web app. I know it’s a big ask but for such an essential app it really should be on the web too. I kind of hate to say it because native apps tend to feel more magical.

5. Minor: can’t reorganize subtasks. Otherwise I love the simplicity of this feature. Properties for subtasks would be too much. Kudos.

Here are the pros!

1. It organizes tasks into a timeline and calendar! Anyone who gets attached to their habits knows that eventually you have to move beyond a simple checklist.

2. Syncs with Apple Reminders! Honestly Apple Reminders is pretty amazing. It’s just missing half of the equation, as many todo list apps are.

3. Procedural task creation!! Very intuitive and a dream to use!! If only it weren’t so laggy.

That’s it! I’m really looking for the task management app that does three key things:

1. Organizes tasks as calendar events
2. Integrates with Google Calendar
3. Allows custom grouping for unorganized and organized tasks

title: Too Bubbly
body:
I’m using Structured because I’ve found it’s the least-worst app for practicing time-blocking with a hectic life and dynamic schedule.

What makes it good is the ease with which you can re-arrange things when you need to, and the ability to capture things without scheduling them — you can drag items down the day, it will show you when things overlap, if you need to move something back to the inbox you can.

What makes it less-than-effective is the amount of screen real-estate dedicated to white space or nonsensical information for the sake of being “pretty”. Someone needs to send their designer to an Edward Tufte course. The widgets are the most egregious example of this — where Things can display five items, this app will display one. On a busy day, one screen on my phone might display about 1.5-3 hours of tasks, with over half the screen lost to margins, circles, and icons. The “Layout” settings offer “Simplified” and “Minimal” which only make the problem worse

I’ve subscribed because I want to give Time Boxing a serious go, and I haven’t found anything else that handles my hectic day-to-day nearly as well. I’m hoping they add a setting (and I’m normally against settings) to provide a “Dense” view, for those of us who like to see more things at once.

A second, less important issue for me is how there are tiny messages commenting on my free time between every single event. Either suggesting I keep it free or to put an event in there. It’s distracting and annoying, and it disrupts how the flow of events in the day looks. I’ll add events if I have events to add, I don’t need a little birdie on my shoulder to tell me to do it.

title: Love it, asking for more
body:
I LOVE this app! It has great day to day features and i like being able to schedule chunks of time instead of by hour (i like categorizing by events in my head instead of time) I’ve been searching all around for this kind of app. Plus, it offers so many emojis for every type of activity and event that other apps don’t, from archery to saxophone. it’s really colorful too. You can even suggest adding other icons to use and it may show up later. I haven’t even fully explored all of it yet. It’s colorful, it’s simple, and it helps you build your week. I’ve been with this app since last summer and it’s amazing so far. 

 However, because of its focus on day to day and week by week events ( which is still a solid ) it lacks a monthly and weekly schedule, where I can see everything I’m doing from a birds eye view. Sometimes I just want to see everything I’m doing that week or month at a glance but I can’t do that on the app, so I often resort to others to make up for it.  Plus the icons underneath each day aren’t sorted by priority or anything so I don’t use it and it takes up space. Maybe add categories to put tasks and events into, so its like ios calendar sorting but more aesthetic. That way I can sort the icons and understand which ones are my day to day tasks, like getting ready and prepping meals, and be able to view by category and only see important events like meeting up with friends or a birthday. I can’t see those kinds of events from the top bar and often have to tap each date individually to check, which is troublesome. Going off of that, maybe change the monthly view so when you press the icon you would be shown the normal monthly view but with select icon categories that you can choose to show up or not. Then you wouldn’t see daily tasks but important events and holidays.

 If features like that can be added to Structured i would pay that $30 no questions asked, because of how much it would benefit my organization and planning for the next few years.

You’re awesome for making this. I see so much potential and would love to see all the new features you add on this app!

title: Stable App, Easiest App for setting times/recurring
body:
I’ve been testing a number of apps recently.
Very pleased with this app. 
Syncs well with my Google Calendar. 
With google calendar, I can only set times in 15 minute increments, and isn’t as easy with scheduling recurring tasks. This app lets you get more specific. 
It’s very easy to set dates, times, recurring, then I can drag items and move them around when I’m looking at the daily schedule.
Very fast response time, I’ve found no buggy behavior that’s makes me hesitate to use this to run my schedule.
Has intuitive features, and also doesn’t auto correct me in such a manner as to get in my way. 
Visually very tidy. 
Will count down how long until a task stars, and how long until done. The color shifts as time passes letting you know where you are in the day. 
Widgets are pretty good, too.

If the devs might ever consider making a display option similar to PiCal, with a clock face, or clock face widget, I’d be in heaven. 

Thanks for the great work.

author: RobertShmurda

title: Should be more popular among the easily distracted
body:
TLDR: Makes it easy to micromanage your time, while looking sexy and most importantly not being overbearing. Why does this sound like my ideal girlfriend? 

Fun stuff aside, personally hold down a 9-5 job, 6-9 uni studies, 11-1 music producer grinds. The schedule bites, but the app helps minimize distractions and is motivating to use.

More nitty gritty:

 UI aligns with research proven techniques like Don't Break the Chain, Visual Timeblocking, Pomodoro, Treating Your Life like a Game

 Visuals help me a lot. EXTREMELY aesthetic and easy to use. Time-blocking in this app surpasses Google calendar by miles. 

 Shows your time spent during the day like sand in an hourglass. As a easily distracted person, this is awesome and relaxing.

 Apple Devices can sync between Structured and Calendars, Reminders. Makes migrating google calendar easy. Routines feature is also dope.

 The iPhone version uses a third party integration called 'One Sec' that slaps.

 The Mac version even has features similar to a Pomodoro.

 More energized to seize the day without being penalized for missing things.

It is clear that a lot of thought went behind the scenes. If you are an easily distracted and visual-dominant person then you'll get a lot of mileage out of Structured.

Thanks Structured Team.

title: SERIOUSLY life changing!
body: I’m the type of person that absolutely needs structure otherwise I end up putting things off and getting nothing done. This app has literally improved my quality of life. I see a few people complaining about there being a subscription but it’s $7.99 for a year, so I don’t see any problem at all helping these folks out. You can use the app without the upgrade, but if you’re trying to take it serious, the upgrade is essential. It takes a little self discipline but I just make sure to schedule some time each Sunday to write everything up for the next week, so that way I don’t end up putting that off too. I also really love how you have the inbox which is where you add things that you’re thinking about, but don’t know any sort of date yet. Things like cleaning out the car, chopping firewood, and all kinds of other stuff. This app is so simple but yet so helpful that I want to tell all my friends about it. If you really want to, you can absolutely change your lazy habits and get in a nice solid routine!

title: You NEED Structured!
body:
Are you a procrastinator? Do you constantly find yourself saying that you’ll have a productive day tomorrow, but you don’t follow through? Have you tried several planner apps that were too complicated, too boring, and too expensive? I know I have- but all that stopped when I downloaded Structured.
Structured is probably the best planner app out there because you don’t have to pay to use it to its full strength, like most planner apps. It gives you access to all of the necessary features, and you only have to pay a little bit if you want all of them. After combing through expensive planner apps for a while, I was absolutely shocked to see that everything was under 2$ a month! I’ve seen like, 10$ a week before, so I’m pretty sure this is the best price you can get.
One of the things I like best about Structured is that it’s really easy to use. The format is clean, the features are well organized, and you can learn how to use it all in five minutes without any tutorial. I’m an idiot and I did.
But you know what the best part is? Structured will get you out of bed, off the phone, and propel you into the work life you want to live. I’ve been more productive- with work, with exercise, with reading, writing, studying, practicing, cleaning, basically anything you can write down that you want to do on a calendar.
(By the way, if the developers are reading this, can you add icons to sub tasks? For some reason, putting those cute little pictures on my tasks makes me want to do them more so I think it would be helpful for sub tasks.)
In conclusion, I’m in love with Structured. I have tremendous respect for the people who developed it, because they have made the first thing that has truly made me productive. Thanks for reading!

title: Almost perfect
body:
When I first came across this app I was starstruck! I had the ability to organize my day with timed tasks, & create future planned tasks. I also like the feature to write needed to-dos without having to set a specific day for this (& assign one in the future) without having to rewrite everything. 

**the reason I switched and use two different apps now..although I paid for the pro version.. 

Although this app has oh so many features I love, it does not currently have a main feature I find useful. ((The search option within calendar view!)) Upon purchasing the pro version I didn’t realize how much it was needed. I like to keep track of certain activities. My memory is not amazing so I rely on this function to keep track of things like upcoming or past events, when I last went to get an oil change, tire rotation etc. 
As of this moment once I enter tasks and complete them.. they are lost in the abyss of the structured app. There is no way of searching when I completed a specific task or when A specific tasks I’m looking for is coming up. I feel like this addition would take this app to the next level and gain it the recognition it deserves. I still have not deleted this app, with the hope it is made a reality. I for one will be converting and getting rid of the other two apps if this feature is added. 🤍

title: Just needs a couple tweaks!
body:
First, if you need to move a task to another time, you have to do a lot of manual adjustments to make it fit. For example, why not let me simply drag my 30 minute 5pm task down to my 2pm slot and bump everything back by the duration of that task? As is, drag and drop is too tedious to use and the other editing options are even more time consuming if your day is any different than you scheduled for. 

Second, I wish you could organize your schedule without the time of day being listed at all. I do pomadoro scheduling for most my day, and it's hard to stay exactly on time, so it's annoying when by the end of my day, the app is telling me I should be at the end of my list when I'm not really that close yet. Just let me organize my day by tasks, and not specific time of day.

App looks great on my Mac, iPhone and Watch and functions well overall. But as someone who is using it morning to night there are a few usability issues that make it quite annoying if anything unexpected at all happens during your day or need to move anything around.

However, it does unlock some icons and more importantly funds the continued development of the app. It’s currently five cents a day. 

I’ve had it for about a month. I chose to write the review now because with 3.0 they added the drag and drop feature, which was the only glaring lacking feature. I’ll also add that I basically swore off productivity apps as useless a few years ago. This is the first one to actually make a difference.

title: love but room for improvement!
body:
I have adhd and have tried MANY planner apps/programs. This one is the best so far in terms of aesthetic and user friendliness, but I have to give it a 4/5 for now because of a few features that are lacking. Would make a huge difference if these could be added!

1) inbox folders: I use the app for both work and personal task/time management, so when I have something that I throw in my inbox to schedule in the future, it ends up looking like a big jumble of work stuff to house chores to side projects and I really wish I could have folders to separate them. I manage now using different colors but there isn’t even a way to reorder the inbox which is annoying.

2) convert between tasks and subtasks: i schedule out my entire day with chunks of time dedicated to work. It would be sooo awesome if I could take tasks from my inbox or the day and turn them into subtasks for specific chunks of work time. That would really help me organize my time. Now I manage by just putting tasks as all day and then retyping them into the work time chunk as subtasks which is very clunky. Would also be nice to have a better visual of subtasks on home page/timeline like side by side so you can see how much time each subtasks takes from the parent task. Would also need some way to convert subtasks back to parent tasks if I need to move things around.

3) weekly inbox: similar to #1, would be so great to be able to have some kind of automatic inbox folder for “next week” and “next month” where you can put stuff in there and then it automatically moves into general inbox when that time comes or something. Or maybe separate inbox at the top as you scroll to each week. (The ability to drag and drop tasks around would help a lot with most of what I am saying)

4) incomplete tasks: so let’s say it’s sunday and I put a bunch of chores on my list for the day but didn’t complete all of them and check them off. It’s really easy to forget after that day that those items are still undone unless I go back to the previous day and reschedule. Wish there was a place for incomplete/overdue tasks - maybe another automated inbox folder

Hope this is helpful!

title: This app deserves 5 Stars… but it needs a few more features.
body:
I downloaded this app yesterday, and it is fantastic. I have ADHD, and being able to put all my to dos and calendars and routine items into one place, viewable on a calendar with checkboxes to tick them off, is AMAZING. Easily worth the annual subscription for the pro version to open up all the features. 

But it needs just a few more:

1) I’d love to see the ability to change the time of multiple events on a given day at the same time: I’m thinking of this as a “edit my day” button that allows selection of multiple events, moving them all together earlier or later in the day. 

2) It would be super helpful to have the ability to reorganize subtasks. I don’t always think of subtasks in order and having them out of order really messes with my head. So I have more than once added in the new subtask I need and then copy and pasted each following subtask below. It’s a unnecessarily cumbersome process. From what I can tell, this could be solved in two possible ways: allow the cursor to create a new subtask when the return key is pushed or the “new subtask” button pressed even if there is a subtask already below, or provide mover bars on each subtask to be able to freely move them within the list. 

3) The icing on the cake would be an option to allow overlapping events when they are 4+ hours long. Maybe a checkbox in the event? This would ideally allow it to stretch beneath other events on the day’s view to help get a feel for what things are overlapping and when to see if they can be worked in or need to be moved. 

Thank you for a great app, and I hope improvements can be made to make it that much better!

Now me personally I hate subscription apps so much so I avoid them? But I thought I would give this app a chance from watching a video on YouTube that this app uses Apple new Live Activity feature. I digress, the face this app allows you buy for a lifetime is something I really appreciate; For less than $30.  I can really appreciate when developers allow to buy the app for a lifetime and doesn’t forget people like me who want to just buy the app just straight out. 

Last thing I love about this app is that you get access to the MacOS version without additional cost by using your ICloud. So I can really appreciate the syncing between my devices to make completing my task seem less experience. If you couldn’t tell already I really love this app give it a try and you don’t need to make a account so everything is as fast as your fingers allow you type.

title: Fabulous App
body:
I stumbled across this app quite by chance this morning when looking into I for on another app I already subscribe to for a different but similar purpose. I was amazed by the number of reviews where users paid for the lifetime subscription and were still asking how to donate additional funds to the dev team because you just don’t see that very often. Furthermore, the lead developer’s description of the latest update was very conversational towards the users-as if he was speaking to a team of employees or a group of friends rather than it being simply technical and distant. Then encourages users to reach out with any issues so they could immediately work on them! Add to that the rave reviews and the app serving a purpose I have needed filled forever - it was a no brainer to download it. 
It is the higher price listed for the lifetime BUT the dev team did include a link if you cannot afford that amount. I don’t know what that does because I went ahead with the list price given how impressive the application is. 
Also, given it allows family sharing I felt the full price was more than fair for lifetime access (for my family it works out to about $7.50 a person, which is amazing (please keep in mind the Family Sharing aspect if you do intend to purchase and are balking at the cost for any level of Premium).
I have been using the app for a few hours and have linked it to my Calendar and Reminders app (the integration has been flawless for me). I love the ability to truly personalize my experience. When we, users, talk and changing the icon color - we mean you can choose from a grid , spectrum, or the sliders in order to customize your colors- it is not just here are 20 or 15 colors to pick from. 
When you open the app there is a brief tutorial which is well done-it is laid out as tasks to complete- took about two minutes.  The subtasks feature is amazing! 
I have been trying to teach my family to block schedule for ages and this app will definitely help-in fact for anyone who block schedules or wants to start or teach it-this is the app to use!!! 
Finally, the dev team has included multiple ways to reach out to them if you have an issue. Additionally, there are ways to submit your logs (yes this is not unique to this app, but it is a sign of a dev team that knows what they are doing and are serious about keeping the app in tip top shape). The team also provided info to empower the user to gain knowledge and resolve issues on their own if possible. The app is simply the complete package! 

Whether you are a homemaker or CEO or Student etc. you need this app in your life - and frankly if you don’t block schedule already-I highly suggest trying it!

title: Better than everything else, but missing key features
body:
This is a first-day review, so maybe these thoughts will change in time. The interface is great, and for the most part highly intuitive. I love the way the connection with local calendars and reminders is implemented, except: I wish you could designate whole calendars and individual events to not be tasks. I use calendars to schedule blocks of time just as frequently as tasks, and it doesn’t make sense for a workday or a multi-day event like a trip to be treated the same as a weekly errand. Something as simple as a blocking/non-blocking toggle with a default value set by calendar that can be changed on an individual basis would be perfect. 

My only other complaint thus far is that the watch app doesn’t seem to update in the background? If it does it’s not as frequently as I wish it did, I went a whole day thinking it didn’t work at all. Other than those, this app is great, it’s almost perfect. If I’m still using it after a month I plan to switch to a lifetime membership.

title: Helps me prioritize and say NO
body:

This app has helped me stay focused, adjust my work schedule (even work less!), say no to things I don’t want to do, and prioritize doing things I actually like. So when I say I don’t have time for drama or scrolling on social media…I literally don’t.

I was using this in the past and stopped because I hated the idea of each minute of my life being tasked. So I switched it up and only have my morning and evening routines scheduled. My day is free to move around as I need, which I’m able to do as a freelancer. It has made me feel less tied to a schedule and rather more disciplined with a routine to help start and end my day in a more peaceful way.

title: (updated)Honest + Structured review 🎖
body:
Oct 2022 edit: Terrific app you made Leo! I remember getting my subscription when this app first came out. 5 stars because you listened to the people. One suggestion I have so far is in minimalist view. I love the idea as I currently have it on, but I do miss the bubbles by the dates on top to let me know I have tasks on those days. I get the whole idea though of "minimalist" but it would be nice if I could toggle that on as an option. Again, thank you Leo! ⭐️⭐️

Beginning of 2022 edit: Works just fine now! Thanks. I'm going back on the 4 star as this app is nearly perfect, it just needs a little touching up. Anyway the first review I made is below. Thank you again! 

Edit: It's been a month since you have updated the app. I would think that an agenda/planner app would have quick updates especially if it starts to crash on initial intake. You know what I mean? Not trying to rush you or anything like that. I know you're a one man brand here so I do feel bad. I'm just trying to get my life sorted out and I thought that an app like this could help. Don't get me wrong, I'm still hooked on its UI. Almost like this app was made for me. Again, I'll wait on the update. 

Edit: Recently, I encountered this app crashing a lot after adding a new task. I deleted the app and reinstalled. Now, almost everything I do, it crashes. I have to make a planner on reminders for now. Until then, I will be waiting on an update 🙂 

First review: So yes this app has helped me in many ways. Let me start off with, this app is life changing in many ways compared to other apps. First and foremost, I love the one time purchase. I think that's very efficient. Here's what should be changed in my opinion. I feel as if there's too many words on the screen "let's plan something for the next x hours" for example. We have the "+" icon on the bottom to add new tasks. Also, a built in light mode dark mode feature would be nice! I think as a young developer Leo, you're doing amazing. I know you're working on the Apple watch version which will be incredible. Life changer again for me. Last thing would be the "inbox" feature. I like the point of it, I just don't find real use for it? Anyway, thank you for your hard work. I have the Mac version also, it's truly great. ❤️

title: Super well-thought-out app for organizing your day
body: I just downloaded this app this week but am really noticing how much thought the developer put into the details. Not only is it great to be able to think about what’s realistic and productive for your day, but there are also lots of ways to customize it depending on your visual preferences. You can choose between a few different “views” depending on if you just like to see the schedule, or if you like lots of detail (like how much time is between tasks). You can set notifications and customize those quite a bit too. There is a lot available to you for free with this app - which is very refreshing. And if you decide to subscribe, the monthly cost is minimal. Even buying a monthly or lifetime membership is not overly expensive! The only thing I would change about this app is to be able to drag tasks or appointments around. As we all know, the day doesn’t always go according to plan, and it would simplify things to have a quick drag-and-drop feature for when that happens. I’ve been noticing that if I don’t get to do things when I had planned, I don’t take the time to go into each one to reschedule it. Maybe other people don’t mind having to do that, but for me, this feature would help a lot.

title: changed my opinion from 5 to 3 stars today
body:
structured

issues 201012

(This comment will be far longer than normal/nec bc I'm kinda hoping someone from Structured will see it and help me since I couldn't find any help online or thru the app...)

SO: Fantastic if you just want to use on its own altho it takes a while to enter calendar items. That is it only takes a little more time than one might like if you just use the default item settings. They give you SO many toys to customize entries tho... if you start taking advantage of those it will take you ages to enter items. 

Love the "hey you have some time free here" reminders etc. and when they're smaller there is an equally fun "break" reminder. As an ADHDer - like others whose comments I've read here - those little free-time snippets REALLY helped me and also made the app just seem so friendly!!... 

On the flip side all the customization options were actually kind of a problem for me - easy to go down rabbit holes of finding the perfect icon, assigning colors to categories etc.... If you can control yourself from that and stick to the defaults you'll be better off - didn't seem to be a way to save new defaults for yourself etc. (You can control the main color, tho.) Still, I love most everything about this app and would keep using it except....

(scary monster music inserted here)...

Today a problem raised its head when I tried to sync Reminders and Structured... I promise I did my Reminders import as directed, but only some reminders are importing, or rather, sometimes they flash on then disappear... doublechecked due dates/times/lists (I've only marked my main list for import - the one where I put due dates). Then I doublechecked I hadn't deleted any etc. but with the two apps side by side, Reminders list for today showing all dates/times correctly, Structured settings accurate for pertinent list, etc., Structured is only showing SOME of those reminders. I then deleted all the ones I had originally created in Structured just in case, to make sure I was only going by Reminders... still showing only some items. Occasionally if I tried to edit a reminder as I was trying to figure out the difference between the ones that were showing and the ones that weren't, an item would appear on Structured for a second and then disappear again... Checked "completed tasks" checked to see if anything was accidentally set for "all day" etc. etc etc 

Went on app and website to search "Reminders importing problems" and as many other ways to refer to the problem as I could think of but nothing would come up - not sure why they have a search feature on there actually - did not seem to be responding to anything I put in at all. Went online to see if the internet public had ideas (that's where I get all my troubleshooting help usually) but because "Structured" is such a generic word (I guess) even putting in "Structured app" or similar would not bring up answers that were specific to the app. 

:( :( :( :( :( 

Really tired of this so I will be turning off my subscription renewal. Super super super super disappointed. I truly thought I had finally found the perfect planner app for my brain. 

I will possibly try Structured again in the future (that should give you an idea of how great it was despite the issues mentioned here - altho you have to turn on Premium and pay for at least a month in order to test importing from calendar or reminders) but it will not be my first reflex.

title: Almost Perfect
body:
I'm writing this after having used Structured for the past 1-2 months to help keep track of the classes I'm team-teaching for (since my schedule is different every week, this app has helped me keep track of the constant changes). With that in mind, I think a few minor improvements would make the app absolutely amazing: 1) Adding 1-2 extra fields for "subtitles" that are visible from the main schedule -- I title my events "1st Period", "3rd Period" etc. to make it easy to duplicate them and keep the same timeslot for my classes. But since I'm often in different classes with different teachers every day/week, it would be nice to be able to "subtitle" each event with a class name (i.e. "Class 2B") and/or instructor name (i.e. "SATO"). I think an upgrade of this type would likely benefit students who use this app for their class schedules as well. 2) Adding a monthly overview/summary view. I'd like to be able to see my upcoming weeks at a glance. A competitive app by Moleskine offers this kind of a view, and I found it helpful for getting my bearings on the kind of workload I'd have in the coming weeks (though it was outrageously expensive so I opted to switch to Structured for that reason).

My only other (minor) complaint is that I purchased the Lifetime Pro version because I was very happy with my initial experience with Structured -- but the Lifetime version does not allow for family-sharing. I wouldn't have been bothered too much by this since the cost was only $10~ USD, but shortly after I recommended it to my husband, sister, and other family members, the Lifetime price suddenly tripled. At that price, it feels a little cumbersome to have every person in my family group purchase their own copy, when it's a fairly light-weight calendar app that doesn't have too many unique features at the moment. However, I'll keep using it in the hopes that the developers will use the money from the higher purchase price to add more features and improve the app constantly.

author: Mrs. Chippy

title: Unique design helps maintian focus and flexibility
body:
Structured is a great application for combining calendar events, reminders, daily or one time tasks into an elegant and easy to use visualization of the day's activities. This is going to be a bit of a long review, but I want to share how I use and integrate the app as well as how I got it working - I had a lot of difficulties at first. A number of reviews mention it as a tool to help with "ADHD" types of organizers, but I also want to comment that it is also a great application for those who are very detailed and organized - it presents your agenda in a unique manner that provides flexibility and is intuitive to how projects get completed. 

I use structured as my daily planner to see what I need to do, what else I have time to do it, and to keep track of what gets done. I add all of my meetings and location-based events to my calendar. I use the calendar for travel time, and to enable me to pull up locations in car play (you can add locations in Structured, but it doesn't work with Carplay (at least not at the time of this review). I reserve reminders for lists (shopping lists, TV show watch lists) and reminders that are in the distant future. Structured is used to pull it all together. I include all of my calendar events but only the distant reminders (lists get placed in the Structured inbox and can make things too busy). I can add tasks to Structured such as habits (take meds, complete repetitive tasks), daily activities, or projects I want to work on to plan out my day. A difference between Structured and a calendar is that the Structured agenda becomes a checklist - so often meetings get pushed back or you decide to work on something earlier rather than later and Structured enables you to mark things off as they are done while still keeping you on track about what's coming up next. Larger projects or someday tasks get added to the inbox. This process enables me to be very detailed about my daily activities and modify them quickly. 
My only cons are 1) compared with reminders is that tasks added to Structured that are not completed, stay with the assigned day rather than rolling to the next day, so you need to perform a daily review and manually move uncompleted tasks to the next day and 2) as another reviewer commented, a search function would be nice to help find something when you may have added it to the wrong date and are not sure which day it was. 

I had some big problems early on - recurring reminders were duplicating (sometimes 12  duplicates), duplicate meetings appearing in Structured but correctly in the calendar, I couldn't get it to work on my watch, The number of agenda items were showing up differently on my phone vs my iPad vs my MacBook. I was very close to giving up on the app but I also saw the many positive reviews and the Structured community was filled with people using it. I liked it enough to continue playing around until I found a solution that worked for me. If you are having issues like mine (I think it's the minority of people) you can try this approach. First, delete the app from all devices and delete the iCloud file (you will loose any data you entered). Reinstall the app on all devices but only allow access to your calendars and reminders using one device (I'm using my phone). After reinstalling and setting it up this way, Structured appears on all of my devices as expected and changes made anywhere are quickly synced with all the other devices. No more duplicates, no more problems.

title: Incredible app. Nothing like it
body:
This app is perfect for anyone who needs a little help organizing daily tasks. It was an immediate purchase for me, plus the developer seems like a really ethical person. 

For example, if $29 is too much for the lifetime subscription, you can write him a reason why you need the app and you may be able to get it for just $10. Idk how this works or if it's just gimmick but it demonstrates a developer solving a problem, not just nickel and diming his audience. 

There are two nitpicks i have. 

1. Recurring events, which are maybe the only reason to really use this app are blocked behind the premium subscription. So guess what, the app isn't free unless you want to manually input each and every daily task one by one. The same goes for reminders and calendar integration. They're nice features but again, locked behind subscription. 

The stock reminders app is ten times more powerful than the free version of this app. I'd take stars away for this but I think the developer is a great role model for others. Btw it's just one person (as far as we know)

2. The widgets would be very useful, but they only show upcoming tasks. This is really not that useful. What I want to see is the list of overdue tasks. That's a lot more sensible and then I can tick off the tasks as I complete them. I'm fact the widgets for this app need an overhaul to really be useful. 

One extra pro for the app: there's a huge roadmap ahead full of incredible features, and you can go and vote on which ones you'd like to see inplemented first.

title: Used it for an hour and I want my money back!
body:
I paid for Pro to access full iOS Calendar and Reminders integration, only to discover the Reminders functionality is half-baked, at best. Reminders with dates already set, or priorities, or pretty much anything else…DO NOT IMPORT!

If you use your Reminders app as nothing more than an inbox for Siri, then rearrange and edit your tasks directly with Structured, then I suppose you might be happy? But the task functionality in this app is NOWHERE near as robust as anything in Reminders, Todoist, or anything else out there. Editing tasks is an exercise in frustration and there is NO WAY to even see a list of upcoming tasks. You have to click on every day for the next year or whatever to find them all. 

On top of all that, the buttons at the top for importing tasks frequency become unresponsive and require the user to restart the app. All this app is really good for is to show you an agenda view of your upcoming appointments. OH WAIT…the default Calendar app already does that. The default app also adds things like a weekly view, yearly view, travel time…OMG SO MANY OTHER THINGS. 

AVOID THIS APP. I am chalking the cost of this “pro” subscription up as a loss and deleting this immediately. 

P.S. Structured does add wake up and sleeping times to your agenda, so if you are really that forgetful, I guess go ahead and use it.

title: Excellent but…
body:
Three stars for attention. The app is excellent and is a massive improvement to my day to day organization, but the planner is missing a couple key features that I feel are sorely missing.

1. Click, hold, and drag feature to reorganize tasks. Sometimes I procrastinate or smthg happens and I lose time. It would be nice to just drag an old task to happen after an upcoming one, and to have all other task rearrange correspondingly, if necessary.

2. Click, hold, and drag tasks from a prior day to the next. Or at the very least a copy and paste button. The current copy button just adds the task to the same day and time. Not very useful.

3. Click, hold, and drag tasks back into the inbox. Sometimes I over schedule, and I need to try again at an unknown later date. Would be nice to just banish these timeless tasks back to the inbox rather than making a whole copy again from scratch.

So, basically I want to be able to drag tasks around so that O don’t have to so much clicking and typing and scrolling when I dont/cant follow the planner to the letter.

Also there’s a weird setup with the scheduling timer with numbers with exponents. Im not sure what the purpose of this is, but I find that if I accidentally trigger it that it becomes the biggest pain to get out of. I think a simple clock timer with a toggled a.m. or p.m. would be easier. If these exponents are supposed to set a task to take up extra days (which is my current guess for this feature, as I haven’t actually needed to even attempt to use it yet), you could just have a “How many days will this task last?” scroll wheel thing instead. Would be less confusing and easier to use.

Again excellent app. Has really helped me “structure” my life better. Just needs a few tweaks for a five star. Even if this review gets no response, Ill update my rating to a four in a couple weeks to better reflect my opinion and help the app gain more traction.

Cheers!

title: Best planner for ADHD
body: I was recently diagnosed with ADHD at 40 years old. I tried too many paper and pen planners and task manager apps to count over the years as I tried to get a handle on time and task management. I found this app about 6 months after my diagnosis, and knowing what I know now about how ADHD brains work, it was almost like it was designed for it. Being able to create timeblocks is essential for visualizing time but being able to check off the task associated with that time--and seeing it remained checked off rather than disappearing once completed--is a fantastic reminder of what I've accomplished during the day given short term memory issues. The app is also attractive and pleasant to use, and I love that it syncs between all my devices because I like to do the planing on my laptop but have it available on the go--as well as the integration with my Apple calendar for appts. It would be great if there were integrations with apps I use for long term task management or project management (such as Todoist), but that is in no way a deal breaker. Overall, Structured is excellent on its own!

title: I am a freelance artist with ADHD and this is perfect
body:
I have such a hard time keeping consistent with my work and having a solid schedule bc it's 100% on me to keep on track. Having ADHD makes that HARD but I've gotta say, Structure has been a godsend. 
It's so well thought out, user friendly, and customizable. I LOVE that I can not only have my task list oranized down to the minute but a todo list WITHIN the task. And checking off those lil boxes just scratch my lil neurodivergent brain in the best way. 
I also LOVE the reminder box for the todos that I want to get done but don't have a specific timeslot for. 
I've used notion, google calendars, notes apps, planners, etc and this by far is my favorite and has everything I need in one place FOR FREE. 
Though, I may get the Pro version (One paymeny of like $9 which is honestly so worth it to me) because you can set it up so your schedule can easily repeat without having to manually input it daily.
The only thing stopping me from getting the pro version rn is bc planning out my next day has become part of my nighttime routine that I am thoroughly enjoying since this is still so new to me. (I've had this app for about a week now).

tldr;
Get this app if you need some Structure in your life. It is so well thought out and helps me keep my ADHD brain on track.

title: Great app, shines on iPad, perfect for ADHD
body:
This is 99% of the perfect app for day planning. Fantastic for ADHD Individuals who tend to get either distracted or hyper focused on things and completely lose track of time (like me). A few features I would like to see added in the future that would make this app perfection:
- the ability to choose what days tasks repeat (i.e. weekday routine items, rehearsals that are on fixed days of the week like Tue and Thu etc)
- in iPad, the ability to drag a task to a time in the timeline view, and a warning that tasks overlap when adding to the timeline (a pop up that says “ This task overlaps with Xyz task that starts at xx:xx’ and give you an option to add your new task within empty time.
- an option to have tasks slide forward on the timeline when adding time to a task or adding a task at a time that overlaps.

Even without these features, this is a true 5 star app. I appreciate that it is functional without a paid version, and that there is a reasonable ‘Lifetime’ purchase option!

This app makes sticking to a routine so easy and you can customize to have as many or as little notifications as you'd like. I also love that the creators aren't baiting people with expensive subscriptions to use basic features and the upgrade is only $10! Highly recommend giving it a try!

title: LOVE!
body:
I really love the Structured app! It’s well worth the $5 for the full version. It’s simple, yet still customizable, but not in an overwhelming way. I love the widget feature and reminders. I downloaded it when I realized my life was passing me by during the pandemic and I needed more structure. It has helped me a lot. (This is not sponsored by the way). 

The only feedback I would suggest are three features that personally would make me enjoy the app even more: 

1. If your phone’s sound is on it would be satisfying to hear a ping or some kind of sound effect when you check a bullet off your planner. This is small, but I just gain satisfaction from hearing chime tones when checking things off of other list apps. If this option is added, the creator can also put it in the settings to turn this feature off for those who may find it annoying. 

2. I think it would also be cool if there was a screen effect of balloons or confetti when you check everything off your list for the day. I know it sounds silly, but I feel like it would make the app more fun and motivating. Similarly to the balloon and confetti effect you can use when using 3d press to send iMessages for iPhone. 

3. If there is a way to be able to incorporate iPhone emojis into the icon chooser when you’re scheduling tasks that’d also be cool. I don’t know if there might be a copyright issue there, but if not, I would love to be able to use iPhone emojis as my task icons in addition to the ones the creator has put on the app :). 

All in all, LOVE, LOVE, LOVE the app as it is. I downloaded a lot of other planner apps to compare to it (ended up deleting them) and this one is still the best for my needs! Highly recommend. Thank you so much to the developer!

title: LOVE THIS, but heads up for Beta users
body:
I love this app so much. I have ADHD and struggle with being overwhelmed by too many calendars, adding tasks/reminders/to-do’s in different locations and then losing them. This app is amazing because it somehow pulls info from wherever I added it (apple reminders, all my calendars, all day events) and drills it down to what I need to do NEXT and what I need to do TODAY. 

I’m the kind of person who needs to put “take garbage out” on my calendar and this app simply and beautifully lets me know that I haven’t done it yet and strikes it out when I did (it’s fun to check off boxes when you did something too).

Great widgets (multiple size options), endless custom colors, and nice interface on the Apple Watch. I wish complications on the watch were a little more varied (being able to see your text task in text/word form instead of just an icon) but I can’t complain about it. It’s nice to flick my wrist and see right away that “call mom” is the next thing unchecked. I don’t have to search for it, it’s just there. 

I bought the full version of this app the second day I used it. It’s just so clean and modern looking. Not TOO many useless options to confuse my ADHD brain, but the options are there if you need/want them. If I had to search for criticisms I would say more/different watch complications would be helpful, and possibly customizable widgets for the phone/iPad. But that’s a stretch - this app is perfect now. 

**iOS 16 Beta**  Widgets do not work which is to be expected but the app still runs fine if you open it. Also does not work on the Beta for Apple Watch. I wish I knew before I committed to the beta testing because I would have honestly preferred the app widgets to work than to see what the new iOS was all about. Just for reference, none of my 3rd party apps are working great on the Beta so this is not an app problem at all. Just a caution to any nerds who want to get this app now but may want to try beta testing down the line.

title: The best planner app ever!
body:
I rarely leave app reviews but I had to for this app.
Key things I love about this app:

1. Buy once, keep it forever: I'm tired of all the subscription-based apps that I'm ready to unsubscribe, and this one definitely stands out for all the great features it offers and still remains non-subscription model. $10 for what it offers is a great deal imo. I hope they don't switch to subscription model for any future versions. I'd rather pay flat fee for upgraded versions. 

2. Cross-platform iCloud Sync: This was the main reason that I ended up choosing this app. I'm used to using Apple's default 'Reminder' app and calendar, and it's wonderful that this app syncs across various platforms and also imports iCal and iPhone's Reminder app. 

3. Intelligent Input: When you're inputting new plan, I just love how it intelligently suggests previously inputted plans that are relevant as well as corresponding icons! It's not always accurate but about 6-70% of the times, the suggested icons match my intent. I really appreciate such attention to details.

4. Time tracker: I love how they chose pomodoro-style linear time tracker - this type of visual que is proven to boost productivity and stay focused. 

5. Overall great UI & Experience: As a designer myself, I think they put a lot of attentions to user interface and experience design (ie. pre / post notifications, etc).

title: BEST for ADHD, OCD
body:
I really really really love this app. As an extremely Type A person who thrives on a tight schedule, this is the best planning app I have ever used, and I've tried so, so many. 

I love every aspect of it! It has the option to color code, import reminders and events from a device's existing calendar, and conditionally move or delete tasks. Its notification system helps to keep me on track when a task begins and ends, and adding the widget to my home screen means that it's never "out of sight, out of mind," but rather always in full view. The little icons for tasks are so cute, and there are so many to choose from. I like that it remembers my previous inputs when adding a new task, making it easy to edit an old option instead of starting from scratch (while making it easy to ignore that suggestion and start from scratch if that's what the moment calls for). 

It really helps me that adding "inbetween" or "transitions" tasks is so easy, meaning I can have BIO CLASS and then LUNCH, but also that I can break down the steps that take me from class to lunch, like "leave class, find car, leave campus, drive home, make lunch, eat lunch, wash up, leave home" -- a super awesome option (on other apps, transition tasks have always looked clunky or difficult to add in. 

I also really love the notes field in each task - the Subtask input. It's so convenient for when I need it, but doesn't show as empty or lacking if I don't mark anything. 

The hourly layout is something I absolutely adore (band kids/drum corps kids who love minute-by-minutes, this is PERFECT), and I love the way it "colors in" the icons as the time progresses. It just makes it to easy to keep track of the day. 

All in all, this is my favorite planning and scheduling app, and I am so so excited to try the mac version.

title: Solid, but missing one feature to be perfect
body:
Great overall, love the inbox feature. Only thing it needs is a force touch-style “touch and drag” to rearrange tasks that automatically bumps the subsequent tasks. 

 For example, if I have “work” from 10-12, “lunch” from 12-1, and “shower” from 1-1:30 — I should be able to touch and hold “shower”, drag and drop it between “work” and “lunch”, and have “lunch” automatically bump back to a new slot at 12:30-1:30. Or, if you add a task during a time where one already exists, it should “bump” the next task back instead of having an overlap. 

 That kind of flexibility/rearranging would save a LOT of time when days change on the fly. Instead of deleting and re-entering and our whole day, you could just drag to rearrange.

Similarly, it would be nice to have a “move all” feature. Let’s say something unexpected comes up in the morning that sets you back 30 minutes — you could just select all tasks and bump them all back.

title: 100/10 - I would recommend to anyone!

I also love that I can pull it up on both my phone and laptop!

The only features I would love to see added/changed are:
-Customized Recurring Events: The app currently allows you to set an event to occur once, daily, weekly, or monthly, with the option to customize to every 1, 2, 3, etc days/weeks/months. I would love the option for the repeated tasks to only ocurr on specific days of the weeks (weekdays, weekends, M/W/F, etc).
-Option to Hide Completed Tasks in the Reminders Inbox
-Option to Change Set Color Options in the Edit Task Window: This is a very small thing, and I can go through a few extra steps to access my favorited colors by selecting a custom color, then clicking "Show Colors," but I would love to be able to add favorited colors in the Edit Task window.

title: The productivity and planning app to rule them all
body:

Rather than 3 or 4 different apps for my calendar, to-do list, schedule and habit tracking, I’ve found that I can use this to do it all. I love the visual timeline of my day. It syncs beautifully with Apple reminders and my Google calendar. 

I started using it because I’m about to have a baby and was stressing out that I wouldn’t be able to keep track of all my persona goals, habits and routines alongside bringing a baby into our household routine. This gives me hope.

Pro tip for those who want to use this as a habit tracker (for habits that happen regularly but not necessarily within a specific time block): create a new reminder list in your Apple reminders, called Daily Habits or something. Add them all in there and set each to repeat as needed. When you sync your reminders with this app, those habits will show up as to-do’s at the top of your daily screen. 

That would be my one feature request for the developers: Add a formal habit tracking feature (like the Strides app) that also allows you to set and keep track of streaks.

title: Amazing! But I need a little more
body:
As a person with ADHD, I have a really hard time adhering my my to do list without a structured plan for WHEN to do the tasks. I also have a difficult time determining how long tasks actually take, so I plan 30 to-dos, thinking that I can accomplish them all, and feel bad about myself when I fail to do so. I’ve tried the time blocking method on my Google Calendar, but I’ve always had trouble sticking to it. 

If you struggle with the same issues, this app is worth checking out!

It is essentially a time-blocking app that integrates your to-dos. What sets this app apart from using Google Calendar and a to-do list is that it shows how far along you are in a specific task/event. It also is extremely visually appealing. It is much easier to use for time-blocking than Google Cal and it just makes more sense for my brain. The widgets are also helpful and beautifully designed.

For only $10, you can integrate your Apple calendar and Apple Reminders app to directly import your events and to-do’s. For a 1 time $10 fee, this is so worth it. Especially because you will have access to the premium features on all of your Apple devices.

The reason why I am giving this app 4 stars instead of 5 is because I can’t actually use it for my needs. I personally use Things 3 as a my task manager and I love it (even though I hardly get everything done because of my time-blindness, lol). I tried moving everything over to Apple Reminders, but I just can’t use it as my primary task manager. I could move what I NEED to do right now over to Apple Reminders, but its just too much work and would take away too much time from actually getting things done.

I also wish that I could directly connect my Google Calendar to the app. I worked around this by integrating my Google Cal with Apple Cal, so that my events import. But if I make any changes to my Google Cal, it takes FOREVER for the change to update on Structured.

If you use Reminders and Apple Cal, this app is incredible. I highly recommend it to anyone, honestly. But I really really really wish that I could use this directly with Things 3. There are probably other people who would like to use this with other apps like Todoist as well. 

I know that this app is developed by one person which is very impressive because it is so amazing and functional. So I also know that is probably really hard for one person to create an integration with Things 3 and other apps. Fingers crossed that this can happen someday 🤞 until then, I can only admire this app from afar 🥺

title: Fantastic!
body:
I pretty much never write reviews but I just had to for how impressed I was with this. Another person with ADHD and autism here. I normally keep my life glued together with Google Calendar and I was pretty skeptical about using another app just for tasks at first. But after a day I realized how useful the set times for each task can be for keeping myself on track. It’s also so much simpler and straightforward than having to add tasks for Google Calendar over and over. I’m actually so grateful for a dedicated tasks app now!
On top of all of that, I was so excited and happy to see the pride icon choices. As small of a gesture they are, I really appreciated them. I hope they’re not taken away after pride month ends.
I’m incredibly impressed by the small team that made this app! The UI is fantastic and I have yet to encounter anything that breaks my experience with it.
Best of all, Pro is just a one time payment. Only $10. Just once. So good! Regardless, even the free mode is perfectly good by itself too.

body:
just started using this app and i have to say, i absolutely ADORE the UI. it’s simplistic and intuitive. i have just a few suggestions. 

1. please add an option to view the whole week and month. i’d like to be able to see my week or month in nice time blocked portions. for example, when i’m on the phone setting up a doctors appointment i’d like to be able to open up my calendar and see what days i’m completely free without having to tap through each day. microsoft’s calendar blocks are similar to what i’m looking for. 

2. please make adding a duration optional. i use this app to remind me of upcoming appointments *before* they happen as well as the actual time they’re at. so it would be helpful to have the duration be optional instead of having to set it to one minute. 

other than that i love this app!

It’s beautiful and fun to use and adds that external motivation that I need to get through the day. Thank you so so much for making this thing - I can’t wait to see what improvements will be made in the future!

Also NO SUBSCRIPTION!!!

I wouldn’t be able to enjoy this app as much if in the back of my mind every time I opened it I thought about how much money I’m spending on it - you made all the right choices for someone with ADD and I appreciate the work so very much! <3

title: Amazing App, could use a couple additions
body:
This app is far and beyond the best thing I’ve found for structuring days and planning things. There are a couple things I would recommend adding that other apps have that this one doesn’t, however.

The biggest one for me is the ability to set when the day starts. I can change my weeks to start Monday, but I can’t set days to start at 2AM. This is aggravating because every time I open the app at work (I work until 1AM and don’t press “sleep” until about 2, when I typically get to bed) it defaults to the next day, and I get confused. Having to press on the “previous day” just seems tedious. The simple solution other apps have is setting when your day begins. This app could greatly use this for people with late night work schedules such as myself.

title: BY FAR the best productivity app available
body: Wow. I am so so grateful for every single thing this app offers. As an off-campus college student with ADHD, and escpecially during COVID with online classes, I have downloaded and tried almost everything I possible could find to help me succeed. I have a four whiteboards just in my bedroom to try to keep me on task and scheduled: calendar, daily planner, ideas and random to-dos, and a reminder daily checklist whiteboard and YOU JUST PUT IT ALL IN ONE APP! It even integrates where I normally put my reminders and calendar events. THANK YOU. I seriously cannot thank the creators enough. Truly from the bottom of my heart, thank you. I can take all four whiteboards with me on my phone, still put my phone on focus modes and get the notification on my watch, not forget about the random meeting I got invited to on Google Calendars that I didn't remember to go put in my calendat, AND I can get a notication when the event ENDS to stay on task! The commute times don't carry over from Apple Maps, so I begin the event when I have to leave anyway, which helps trmendously. This is what immediately opens when I open my MacBook and is essential to helping me especially with the color fade feature. I ACTUALLY teared up after a few days of using it because my stress levels were so low. I have a reminder to double check the following  day is planned and I enjoy doing it for myself. I will be highly reccomending this everywhere and trying to give you all of the support that I can, because you have helped me enormously. THANK YOU. The other indie apps that you reccomend I will also be downloading and reviewing. I look forward to using this app all day and am overflowing with appreciation for you and your team. THANK YOU.

I would not have spent $10 on something that not only didn’t function as promised but had zero response from “support”.  

2. I am constantly bombarded all day long with notifications five minutes before at the time of the event at the end of the event for everything that happens all day. It is extremely annoying. I have checked that I only wanted to be notified five minutes before each item on my days list. These notifications cannot be removed. You cannot choose just one.  It will give you all three no matter what you tell it. So instead of helping me to stay on schedule and on task, it is distracting and annoying. I end up being more confused rather than less confused about my schedule. 

I don’t understand the high rating for this app at all. There are other issues but I thought these were the two most important ones for now.

title: need just a few more upgrades
body:
i just got this app yesterday to start planning my days on my phone and laptop, some things that need adjusting though are small but would make the app even more efficient and maybe even better than everything else out there! 
    1) there should be a monthly detailed calendar. what i mean by this is there should be a way to zoom out to the month and see what days have plans so you are able to see your free days or when you work, etc!
    2) once you rate the app, you shouldn’t have to be asked to rate it anymore. i have gotten spammed quite a few times to rate the app even though i did rate it!
    3) you should be able to type in color codes for themes and color swatches you can choose! meaning you can get a code like html, rgb, and hsl values to get that exact color easily so you can set better color themes!
    4) you should have a widget! so you can see your updates through your phone without opening the app.
    5) you should be able to take and add subscription codes to grab or drop plans from calendar to calendar. it’s quite annoying to plan everything here and not be able to copy and paste the plans to another calendar just in case.
    6) last, you should be able to share the calendar with others wether it be a pdf or layout for others to see your schedule! 
thank you so much and i hope you enjoy this feedback, i usually don’t give any to anyone but i see true potential for this app, i also love the pink!! so much!!

title: You need this app right now.
body: This app has been a God send. I am a disabled college student who works part time. One of my disabilities has made my short term memory absolutely terrible. It’s so bad that I have 5 different calendars to keep up with everything I need to. But I’ve never found a calendar that structures things in a way that helps me remember what I need to. I could create a bullet journal (so I can fully customize it) but I don’t have the time. So I’ve been scouring the App Store and the internet trying to find a system for me. Then I found Structured. No only is it super simple to use, the layout is perfect for me. It shows your full day laid out by time, it fills up the task with color as time passes during that task, and it tells you how much time you have between tasks so you know what you have time for! One of my favorite parts is the Inbox area where you can put tasks you have that you don’t technically have a due date or specific time for. It’s just a task that needs to get done. I love that because now I can simply type things out that I know I need to get done, before I forget about it. You can also set it as a widget on your Home Screen. There’s much much more that I love but this review is way too long already! Just know you need to get this app. Don’t question it. Just get it.

title: Great for Visually Driven People with ADHD
body:
I’m a very busy professional who has to battle ADHD with 9 to 12-hour workdays. I have tried virtually every form of written and electronic planner/task list—I’ve even created my own. This is the best thing I’ve found that incorporates my needs without requiring far too many hours of my own time to setup and maintain. 

Things I like:
• ability to color code tasks with colors you set on your own
• importing appointments and tasks from iPhone/Mac reminders and calendars 
• backup to iCloud so the tasks are seamless on iPhone, iPad, and MacBook 
• adding icons to tasks 
• moving tasks back and forth between an unplanned “inbox” and a planned day 
• being able to add subtasks and notes (including links)  to each task
• you can change the appearance to any color you want 

Features I wish this had:
• ability to designate a time estimate for each subtask 
• more icons or ability to add your own
• dragging and dropping tasks to new dates/times
• ability to share tasks with others (this would be particularly helpful for people like me who have different iCloud accounts for home and work or who collaborate on tasks)
* ability to attach documents to tasks
* ability to make the Inbox tab wider.  

Despite my long, picky wishlist, this is, in fact the closest to a perfect app I have found so far.

title: Is this... the one?
body:
Ok productivity / timeblocking nerds: if you use iphone/apple/ios, i recommended checking out Structured (free, or one time $9.99 to upgrade to synch w google calendar/outlook   reminders which is totally worth it). I get no kickback from this, I’m genuinely just really happy i found it!
It really helped me have a fulfilling weekend!  With the start of my very intentional six-week career break I wanted some way to keep me focused, encourage me to plan ahead, and be more intentional about using my time off wisely – – not just to be “productive” but also to plan my  leisure time well! But also i scheduled myself to apply for a particular new job at a particular time today and … i actually did it at that time?!?!. What magic is this?
This app is super pleasing to use and shockingly effective for me so far. Way cheaper than the useMotion app that Facebook kept pushing on me.  Free (or $9.99 one-time fee to upgrade) vs. $19 a month for useMotion! (In fact it was while researching useMotion, watching a frustrated video reviewer struggle with it, that i read about the Structured app from video commenters!)￼.   One of the coolest things I've found is the integration not only with calendars but with the Apple Reminders app -- an app that I had previously given up on using but Structured supercharges it.  Like I ride my bike with my iphone mounted to my handlebars, and will often have random thoughts like "oh I need to buy bread".  So I say "hey siri, remind me to buy bread" and it creates a reminder that also becomes a task in my Structured "inbox" which is essentially a backlog of tasks not assigned to a date/time.  Even cooler, if I say "Hey Siri, remind me to call Janet at 7pm tomorrow" the reminder app integration will actually schedule the task for tomorrows date at 7pm!  This is insanely awesome

title: Issues, missing features, nagging
body:
Since I purchased this today and first used on my iPhone then my Mac, I've already noticed issues and missing features and regret this purchase. 

First, I cannot enter two tasks in a row on the Mac without getting another nag screen to review this app. This is after having purchased a lifetime pro version. So here's your review, Structured developers. 

Secondly, there are issues and missing features that make this not so great. On a Mac, when I try to enter a new In Box task, that's Shift Command N. However, right after entering a new to-do task, I cannot use the same command to enter another one without first clicking on the app with the cursor. One should be able to continue entering tasks uninterrupted without having to do this. Basic functionailty fail. 

Another issue on the iPhone version is that scheduling a task is a hassle. If they have tasks automatically starting at a certain time, you have to tediously scroll through the times. If you're then ahead of the time of the end of the task, that will then bump the start time to a different hour. It can be a hassle to get the time straight on the phone. 

Inbox tasks and other tasks seemingly have NO way to enter a priority! This is a huge issue if you have a huge to do list like I do. No priority at all. So you'll have a very long inbox list of tasks with no way to sort them by priority or due date. What a mess!

In the less than an hour since I've purchased, I've already noted these major missing features and lack of functionality. Doubt I'll stay with the product due to these issues. I very much regret this purchase.

The one-time upgrade to Pro was a no-brainer. I look forward to supporting the developer through improvements and new apps they may build!
